events.title: NVIDIA Cosmos Opens New Tools to Train, Evaluate and Deploy World Models
events.summary: To help developers rapidly build world models , which help physical AI systems understand and simulate the real world, NVIDIA has expanded the Cosmos platform with new training tools, simulation checkpoints and Cosmos Data Factory blueprints. Ranking top five on six different open models leaderboards, the NVIDIA Cosmos platform gives world model builders the frontier open models — as well as data, training and optimization tools and recipes — to scale training data, adapt models, test behavior and optimize for performance before deployment. Building world models begins with multimodal, multisensory data. NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory brings together the tools and skills for labeling, curating, augmenting and evaluating data at scale for training physical AI. Cosmos Curator, a GPU-accelerated solution for curating video training datasets, has now added support for multimodal multisensory inputs and processing blocks. Cosmos Data Factory now offers the following five cloud-native blueprints and is available through GitHub , Microsoft Azure , Nebius and CoreWeave : Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation: Curates and labels driving data, then adds synthetic examples of hard-to-capture scenarios to expand training coverage. Image Attribute Augmentation: Varies object appearance to improve image search. Event Video Generation: Turns still images into synthetic videos of rare or unsafe events. Defect Image Generation: Generates printed circuit board, metal and glass defect images for inspection models. Video Data Augmentation: Changes weather and lighting in existing footage while preserving scene structure. Cosmos Data Factory accelerates data curation, processing and synthetic data generation with agentic skills. Companies are already putting Cosmos Data Factory blueprints to work to speed their physical AI development workflows. Porsche is leading the development of a shared AV data flywheel across Volkswagen Group brands, using Cosmos Data Factory through Voxel51 on Microsoft Azure. This is expected to reduce repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shorten development cycle times by up to 85%. Porsche searching and augmenting autonomous vehicle data footage in Voxel51, powered by Cosmos Data Factory. ANYbotics generated over 1,500 synthetic video clips with Cosmos Data Factory blueprints, curating real-world data and validating outputs with Encord’s platform, to train its industrial-inspection robots to recognize liquid spills and other changes between facility visits. ANYbotic s generating anomaly clips with Encord powered by NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory. Ultralytics , a computer vision company, retrained its YOLO model with real images and targeted synthetic defects generated using Cosmos Data Factory, improving defect localization and recall. With training data prepared, developers may train their own architecture or start with a pretrained model. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA extended Cosmos Framework training, optimization and deployment tools and recipes as agent skills to more open models, along with Cosmos 3, giving world model builders a faster path from experimentation to deployment. Developers and agents can now adapt open models like GR00T , Alpamayo , QWEN, Pi0.5 and other compatible Hugging Face models through fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, optimize the model with distillation and quantization, and deploy with high-performing inference. To develop a world model specialized for egocentric manipulation, robotics research lab MicroAGI post-trained Cosmos 3 on videos of humans manipulating objects and distilled its 32-billion-parameter reasoner down to an 8-billion-parameter Nano model with no loss in accuracy. Developers can label data and post-train Cosmos 3 on Roboflow for their specific environments and tasks, then deploy those models to RoboFlow hosted or on-premises NVIDIA GPUs to bring video reasoning into factories and warehouses. Test Policies and Run Models Faster Alongside these tools, NVIDIA continues advancing foundational technology through its work on Cosmos models. New Cosmos 3 Nano model variants for simulation enable developers to test autonomous policies in repeatable, hard-to-capture, multiview multisensor scenarios. Accompanying code allows developers to adapt the models to train and evaluate their own policies for autonomous vehicles and bimanual robots in interactive simulations before real-world testing. Developers can deploy core Cosmos models using updated NVIDIA Cosmos 3 NIM microservices, which deliver up to 2x faster inference with no quality loss in validated configurations, while continuous video analysis enables sub-second alerts. For vision AI developers, the new NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) 3.3 , built on Cosmos NIM microservices, turns one prompt into an efficient video AI application and helps teams monitor 40% more video streams with the same GPU. ADNOC uses Fogsphere’s MistIQ agentic platform , built with Cosmos and the NVIDIA Metropolis VSS Blueprint , to detect safety hazards in real time across 65 sites. For rare events, Fogsphere also uses the Cosmos Data Factory to generate synthetic training data, improving detection without needing to physically stage dangerous situations. The Cosmos platform is fully modular and open. Developers can use Cosmos Data Factory to generate training datasets, Cosmos Framework to train and adapt world models, then deploy supported Cosmos models through NIM microservices . events.title: How Companies Are Using NVIDIA DSX to Break the Power Bottleneck
events.summary: Companies around the world are building on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform to plan, simulate and run the grid and the AI factory as one system, from the substation to the rack. Their adoption of the platform responds to an acute problem. Power is now the biggest bottleneck in infrastructure. More than $300 billion in equipment is backlogged, and over 200 gigawatts of projects are waiting in U.S. interconnection queues. One root cause of the bottleneck is siloed systems. The grid, the facility and the compute inside have long been designed independently from one another, creating the conditions for delays, risk and stranded capacity. To help address this, NVIDIA DSX brings these systems together: NVIDIA DSX Sim and SimReady assets from leading energy manufacturers let engineers simulate the grid, substation and AI factory together, validating generators, switchgear, power systems and cooling before breaking ground. NVIDIA DSX Flex syncs AI factory demand with grid conditions and onsite generation, turning AI factories from static loads into flexible grid assets. NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS and DSX Exchange squeeze more compute from every watt and securely share signals across compute, networking, energy, cooling and operations. GE Vernova is deploying its grid-to-facility and rack power expertise to complement NVIDIA DSX systems, enabling customers to transform power constraints into competitive advantages while maximizing compute and token output, sustainability and grid reliability. Hitachi Energy ’s battery energy storage system has qualified as NVIDIA DSX Ready , helping customers identify power infrastructure that meets applicable NVIDIA DSX reference architecture design requirements for resilient, reliable and scalable AI factories. Schneider Electric , together with AVEVA and ETAP, is advancing NVIDIA DSX with validated NVIDIA Vera Rubin power and cooling reference architectures and an NVIDIA Omniverse -powered AI factory digital twin. Combining AVEVA ’s engineering software expertise with NVIDIA SimReady assets, OpenUSD and Omniverse enables connecting simulations, real-time operational data and AI-driven optimization across AVEVA, Schneider Electric and third-party solutions. Together, these capabilities help organizations design, simulate, operate and optimize data centers across their lifecycle, improving energy efficiency and workload performance while accelerating time to token. Siemens Energy is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA by developing a reference design for resilient, scalable and grid-aware power infrastructure across power generation, transmission and distribution. This design is aligned with the requirements of the NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factory design. The company is also exploring usingNVIDIA technologies such as RAPIDS, Metropolis and Isaac Sim for its Noedra digital twin platform, evaluating how the technologies could enhance grid infrastructure monitoring, identify emerging risks and support unplanned outage prevention. Phaidra integrated DSX Flex, DSX Max-Q and DSX Exchange into its self-learning agents, optimizing cooling and power allocation to maximize tokens per watt, improve grid flexibility and deliver about 10% more compute within the same power envelope. Emerald AI integrated its Conductor platform into DSX Flex to help utilities tap underused grid capacity, an approach modeled to unlock up to 100 gigawatts on the existing U.S. grid. Explore the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint and the Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory Reference Design . Learn more from NVIDIA and energy leaders who are accelerating power-flexible AI factories to strengthen the grid at GTC Berlin. Visit Hitachi Energy (booth 7004, hall 7), Schneider Electric (booth 3041, hall 3) and Siemens Energy (booth 3048, hall 3) and tune into sessions with Schneider Electric on Wednesday, Oct. 21: From Grid to AI: Engineering the Future of AI Factories and Energy Intelligence: Powering the AI Era . events.title: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations
events.summary: European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D. Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, NVIDIA CCluster vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations. Zooplus , Europe’s leading online pet retailer, with Infosys and NVIDIA technologies rebuilt its product discovery stack for the agentic era. A production ready prototype deployed inside Zooplus ’ Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment achieved 86% search accuracy using the NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever library for semantic search and the NVIDIA Blueprint for retail catalog enrichment for generated, search-ready product attributes. Photoroom results from its deployment with Vestiaire Collective , where its Image Editing API now standardizes every primary image, about 40,000 a day across 70 countries, at the point of listing. Listings processed by Photoroom sold at a 5% higher rate of liquidity, with 3% to 7% more unique views per product page . The pipeline runs on NVIDIA GPUs with TensorRT and Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo Snapshot can help users quickly respond to demand spikes. Omi launched ProductDrop, a workflow that anchors every generated image to an approved digital twin, letting brands scale creative output across entire catalogs without introducing product errors . L’Oréal is using this approach, combining Omi ’s digital twins with generated brand environments within its CreAItech program. Omi runs TRELLIS 3D asset generation on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, speeding up inference by 10x and reducing pipeline latency by 4x. In addition, L’Oréal is accelerating the discovery of the best ingredient combinations, moving from months of experimentation to hours of computational screening, with the integration of NVIDIA ALCHEMI into its research workflow. L’Oréal is also testing this approach with CurieOS, Orbital Industries ‘ operating system for science and engineering, using OrbMol-v2, its open source molecular simulation model. Integrated with the NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit and powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, OrbMol-v2 is five times faster than comparable models and delivers 21% lower error than the next-best model of its kind. This AI-based workflow enables researchers to identify the most promising ingredient combinations for solubilizing UV filters and optimizing performance before committing to laboratory testing. Mirakl , a software company for intelligent commerce, runs open models on NVIDIA GPUs, both on its own infrastructure and through European cloud providers like Scaleway . This keeps its technology sovereign, avoids vendor lock-in and delivers the speed and scale its customers expect . Mirakl ’s Catalog Transformer pairs fine-tuned open models with proprietary services and has onboarded more than 70 million products, turning messy vendor data into accurate, well-organized catalogs. Physical Intelligence Enables Training in Simulation NVIDIA physical AI, digital twins and open models help simulate retail environments, automate warehouse operations and deliver virtual try-on experiences for European retailers and fashion brands. Otto Group advanced its autonomous warehouse under human supervision initiative — built with Reply on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and running on Google Cloud — to the group’s largest fulfillment center in Haldensleben, Germany. New capabilities let logistics teams design, test and optimize warehouse operations entirely in simulation before any physical implementation . ALLSIDES launched its 3D Digital Twin Factory: an automated pipeline that transforms physical objects into SimReady 3D digital twins in minutes, capturing sub-millimeter geometric accuracy, measured physical properties and fully relightable materials that maintain accuracy under any lighting condition. Those digital twins serve as the foundation for simulating entire store layouts in 3D, as well as for tracking products reliably throughout the shopping journey and at checkout regardless of ambient light. Built on NVIDIA CUDA, OptiX and TensorRT, the platform already serves brands including adidas , Amazon , Nike , Zalando and Zara . CATCHES achieved production results from its RealFit deployment with AMIRI of conversion up 55%, add-to-cart up 80% and gross sales up 56% , all after seasonal adjustment against like-for-like styles. The company launched PredictiveFit, extending physics-based virtual try-on to retailers, as well as CASI, a personal fashion agent that shops, styles and sizes for customers over WhatsApp, powered by open weight models including NVIDIA Nemotron 3, built on NVIDIA Omniverse and the Newton Physics Engine. Explore New NVIDIA Retail Blueprints at the Nebius Booth At GTC Berlin, Nebius is showcasing three NVIDIA Blueprints for retail , all available in early access and running on Nebius infrastructure, accelerated by NVIDIA: Agent Harness for Employee Productivity : An agentic assistant that consolidates scheduling, task management, inventory alerts and operational insights for store managers. Inventory Simulation and Optimization: A blueprint that can help retailers reduce overstock and stockouts by modeling demand scenarios, testing replenishment strategies and optimizing stock levels before users need to commit in the real world. Agentic Finetuning Flywheel: A self-improving loop that uses agentic workflows to continuously generate training data, fine-tune open source models and feed real-world performance back into the next training cycle. events.title: Pioneers Across Europe Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 Open Models to Power Real-World Weather and Climate Prediction
events.summary: Weather forecasts shape more than daily plans; timely weather information is crucial for energy producers, insurers and transport operators to plan around changing conditions. A global forecast can show a storm taking shape, but decisions about solar farms, shipping routes or insured property depend on what happens locally. NVIDIA Earth-2 gives developers and researchers a family of open AI models and tools they can customize with their own data. Running on NVIDIA computing, these technologies support global weather prediction, detailed regional forecasts and environmental research. StormScope EU is the latest model to join Earth-2 — a regional version of the StormScope model for short-term forecasting, trained over Europe weather and climate data. It uses EUMETSAT satellite observations to predict evolving cloud conditions across 16 Meteosat channels at 10-minute intervals. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing a live StormScope EU pipeline in an interactive weather demo built in partnership with Earthmover . The demo uses Earth2Studio to run forecasts and Earthmover’s data platform to manage and serve the real-time results, which are updated as soon as new satellite observations come in, every 10 minutes. Earthmover serves these results as map tiles, letting visitors explore predictions across Europe without downloading entire datasets. Developers can combine Earth-2 models in workflows tailored to regional needs, using StormScope for short-term forecasting and CorrDiff to add local detail to coarser weather data. Developers can also pick up these model architectures and train them for new environmental applications such as air-quality modeling. The open source NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo framework provides training and customization tools so teams can build applications that incorporate proprietary data and domain expertise to meet regional needs. Organizations building on Earth-2 capabilities include: AXA is using NVIDIA Earth-2’s FourCastNet 3 to study regional cyclone risk beyond the historical record across more than 1,000 simulated seasons, generating insights that can inform risk assessments and help customers target prevention efforts. Vaisala Xweather is combining Earth-2 with its proprietary observations , lightning data and forecasting expertise to enhance its weather intelligence platforms for government, energy, maritime, transportation and insurance customers. Its work includes adapting StormScope with lightning data to advance short-term forecasting lead time and make these warnings accessible through Vaisala Xweather’s software-as-a-service offerings and AI-assistant integrations. Video courtesy of Vaisala Xweather. University of Manchester researchers adapted the Earth-2 CorrDiff model for U.K. air-quality modeling. It trained the model on the NVIDIA-powered Isambard-AI supercomputer and ran it locally on NVIDIA DGX Spark systems, bringing environmental modeling from a national supercomputer to the desktop. TotalEnergies is exploring NVIDIA Earth-2 for solar-energy forecasting, evaluating StormScope-based solar-radiation nowcasts at two photovoltaic sites and developing models to provide weather information at subhourly intervals. The work explores how more detailed forecasts could help anticipate changes in solar-power generation. Space42 developed SARDiff4Height using CorrDiff and NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo. The research estimates surface heights from a single radar image and produces uncertainty maps, helping analysts understand where estimates need closer scrutiny. Explore NVIDIA Earth-2 open models and tools , and explore with Earth2Studio’s forecasting examples . Read AXA’s hurricane-risk case study and Manchester’s air-quality story to learn how teams are adapting weather AI to specialized challenges. events.title: NVIDIA Open Models Power a New Wave of European Public Sector Projects
events.summary: Governments need modern solutions to serve the public while keeping sensitive information under their control. Open models provide a path forward, letting governments evaluate them, adapt them to local languages and public services, run them on infrastructure they control, apply their own safeguards and keep sensitive data within controlled environments. Some open models go further, with the datasets they were trained on published so governments can verify if training data was licensed, biased or compliant. NVIDIA partners and European governments are teaming to bring advanced models to boost the efficiency of public administration while retaining control of data and infrastructure. Several are also building editions of the NVIDIA Nemotron-Personas collection , the partner-grounded datasets behind NeMo User Sim , NVIDIA’s open source library for population-scale user simulation that dynamically evaluates and trains models and agents in local languages. European Commission: Scaling Governed AI Applications Berlin-based software company deepset is expanding its Haystack Enterprise Platform , the foundation of AI@EC, the European Commission’s shared platform for building and running AI applications on commission-managed infrastructure. The update connects agent development, execution, optimization and governance for all customers, adding capabilities to compare operating costs, evaluate answer quality and trace problems. NVIDIA Triton Inference Server supports the shared services used to find and rank relevant information. The expansion builds on operating requirements demonstrated by deployments such as AI@EC, where reusable components, role-based access, audit trails and guardrails support applications including document summarization, knowledge management and multilingual policy analysis. Poland: Advanced Computing for Healthcare and Employment Deloitte is helping Poland build agentic systems for healthcare and employment services using open models. Poland’s eHealth Centre is building its Intelligent Services Platform for medical imaging with NVIDIA DGX BasePOD and the MONAI framework. The tool will help physicians analyze X-rays, CT scans and MRI images, detect abnormalities and prioritize urgent cases, reducing the time patients wait for results. With Deloitte’s support, Poland’s Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Policy is developing an agentic factory on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure. Designed to support more than 400 labor offices, it will run models including PLLuM, GPT OSS and Inkling for document search, summarization and digital assistants, helping staff more efficiently assist job seekers. NVIDIA is also working with SpeakLeash in Poland and the University of Ljubljana in Slovenia on country-specific additions to its synthetic personas program, with localized datasets planned to follow. UK: Data for Locally Relevant Advanced Modeling London-based Locai Labs released Nemotron-Personas-UK , a dataset of 1 million synthetic personas reflecting the U.K.’s demographic and geographic diversity while reducing privacy risk. Potential uses include healthcare evaluation and bias testing across age groups, education levels and rural and urban populations. For developers building public-service models, it offers a way to test whether models work consistently across different communities. Germany: Digital Assistants and AI for Classified Work In Germany, Materna is introducing Sinfonie, an on-premises platform combining generative AI, voice interaction and 3D avatars, with NVIDIA Audio2Face available for animation. Built on a project for a German state administration, it helps employees access institutional knowledge through spoken questions while keeping data on their organization’s infrastructure. For organizations handling classified information, secunet, NVIDIA, Red Hat and deepset are going a step further. The four companies are developing a sovereign cloud offering built on secunet’s proven SINA Cloud foundation, which includes security components that have been authorized for use with classified information. The planned offering combines four components: NVIDIA accelerated computing and NVIDIA Nemotron open models; Red Hat OpenShift AI for deploying and managing AI workloads; deepset’s Haystack AI agent orchestration; and infrastructure operated by secunet in German data centers. To support local development, the Sovereign Open Source Foundation Models research initiative (Soofi) is developing a family of AI models for German industry and the public sector. That includes Nemotron-Personas-Germany, an open dataset of 1 million records, each with six synthetic personas, grounded in the 2022 census across all 16 federal states and 400 districts. Created with NVIDIA NeMo Data Designer without real people’s private data, the dataset helps developers test whether public-service models work consistently across regions, age groups and communities. Like the U.K. edition, it can be used with NeMo User Sim so developers can evaluate and train models against simulated users based on synthetic German personas. France: Advanced Open Models in the Public Sector Workspace CANUT, France’s public purchasing body for digital services, selected LINAGORA and Docaposte to provide a sovereign collaborative workspace built on Twake.ai. More than 2,500 eligible organizations, including municipalities, schools and healthcare institutions, can access the framework without running their own tender. The workspace offers public employees email, document sharing and collaboration tools, with NVIDIA technology supporting speech transcription and infrastructure hosted in France. Région Occitanie is the preferred partner for scaling deployment. Greek AI and energy company KIEFER is developing an agentic factory built on NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD with DGX GB200 alongside Sophea open weight models and Greek-language tools for knowledge retrieval, speech and digital assistants. These capabilities stand to make institutional information easier to find and use for Greek-speaking public sector teams, while giving organizations control over where agents run and how data is handled. Codefest: Building the Next Applications In an effort to support public sector organizations in integrating agentic AI in Europe and beyond, NVIDIA Open Models Codefest brings together startups, software providers and labs across the region to turn open models into locally controlled solutions for public sector challenges, including medical reasoning, AI tutoring and model governance. The top five teams are Pleias , Zehnlab.ai , Disseqt , Algoritmica GmbH and ABA Technology . Deutsche Telekom and T-Systems have provided the compute infrastructure for teams to train and deploy large language models. events.title: Oil tops $110 as Houthi drone strike near Saudi Shaybah field rattles markets
events.summary: Oil extended gains above $110 a barrel on Thursday after a Houthi drone attack near Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield heightened concerns over supply disruptions as Yemen's rebels stepped up strikes on the kingdom's energy infrastructure. Brent crude rose 1.7 per cent, or $1.81, to $110.63 a barrel as of 7.36am UAE time. West Texas Intermediate gained 1.4 per cent, or $1.37, to $98.52. Two people were killed and two injured on Wednesday when debris from a drone intercepted by Saudi air defences fell near a processing plant at Shaybah, one of the kingdom's largest oilfields. The drone targeted the plant, but its debris struck a contractor's vehicle outside and caused a fire, the Saudi Energy Ministry said. Operations were unaffected. Shaybah, deep in the Empty Quarter near the UAE border, produces about one million barrels of crude a day. The strike came hours before another attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one person and injured eight, according to Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority. The Houthis have not commented on the airport attack. The latest strikes follow an attack on Riyadh's main international airport earlier this month, the deadliest on the kingdom in more than a decade. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline , a critical alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, has also come under attack. Crude flows were reportedly halted on October 5 after a Houthi strike damaged a pumping station east of Riyadh. The pipeline, which has a capacity of about seven million barrels a day, carries crude from the kingdom's eastern oilfields to Red Sea export terminals, allowing shipments to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. Washington has ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, citing Houthi attacks on civilian airports and critical infrastructure. The widening campaign is adding to the geopolitical risk premium in oil prices as attacks threaten Saudi production facilities and alternative export routes already strained by the Iran war.

events.title: Coastal construction projects threaten the mangrove forest that protects Vietnam's biggest city
events.summary: Construction projects are putting at risk a mangrove forest that stands between Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City and rising seas CAN GIO, Vietnam -- Mangrove forests, a vital buffer between Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City and an increasingly volatile sea, are at risk as the country's financial capital expands and construction reshapes its coastline. For generations, a dense tangle of mangrove trees has shielded the city as rising temperatures due to climate change intensified storms and flooding. Their roots knit the coastline together, sheltering marine life and fish and absorbing carbon emissions. Scientists warn that construction of Can Gio, a new seaside city, along with a major port, roads, bridges and a 14-km (9-mile) sea-crossing route between Can Gio and the port city of Vung Tau, could disrupt water flows that sustain the mangroves, weakening a natural defense for the city of 10 million. Ho Chi Minh City, formerly known as Saigon, is one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable cities . About 80% of its area is vulnerable to flooding, a 2026 study by Vietnamese scientists found . Even now, the government estimates that rising seawater costs the city about $57 million a year. In 2025, record downpours and the highest tides in its history flooded streets and homes. The mangroves in Can Gio nearly died out during the Vietnam War , when U.S. forces sprayed chemicals to strip away cover for Viet Cong guerilla fighters. In the late 1970s, the forest was painstakingly replanted. It became Vietnam’s first UNESCO biosphere reserve in 2000. As Vietnam pushes to become Asia’s next tiger economy , it is transforming its 3,260 kilometer (2,030 mile) coastline. In April, the country's largest company, Vingroup , broke ground for the new coastal town on reclaimed land the size of 1,800 soccer fields. Authorities view Can Gio as a “gateway to the sea” and vital logistics hub. Its new $4.7 billion port will handle millions of shipping containers a year. It's also slated to become a major tourism destination. At the heart of those plans is Vingroup's Green Paradise — a 2,870-hectare (more than 7,000 acre) coastal development the conglomerate’s property arm, Vinhomes, is building. It will include housing, shopping and entertainment areas. Along with the crossing to Vung Tau, Vingroup is working on a metro line connecting Can Gio to Ho Chi Minh City and roads that will link to the city’s expressway network. Life in the fishing town of Can Gio has long followed the tides and seasons. Legends tell of whales that saved imperiled fishing boats. Small shrines devoted to local deities dot the forest. Residents are divided. Many rely on fishing, and the construction has pushed fish into deeper waters beyond the reach of their small boats. over livelihoods tied to the mangroves. Now fisher folk look on as concrete seawalls and embankments steadily enclose reclaimed land. Massive pipes and bulldozers line the beach. But many younger people now work for Vingroup. Some hope the projects will bring more jobs, while others complain they received scant compensation for land now being marketed for far more. Muoi, who gave only one name for fear of reprisals by authorities, gave up fishing and now helps his wife in her shop. Blocked drainage has worsened floods and polluted the water, killing oysters and wiping out farms, Muoi said. Can Gio was once “magical,” he said. “That doesn’t exist anymore. They have boarded everything up.” The mangrove forest's mature trees and carbon-rich soils store earth warming greenhouse gases, said Marie Arnaud, a researcher at the French Sustainable Development Institute based at the Sorbonne University in Paris. “Can Gio is quite important to Vietnam,” she said, citing the project’s huge scale as a concern. Apart from disruptions to water flows, increased pollution will add to pressures on the ecosystem, she said. Rep. In Colombia’s Ciénaga Grande, roads and dikes disrupted the flow of seawater and freshwater from the 1950s onward, contributing to one of the largest mangrove die-offs on record. Globally, a net 284,000 hectares (702,000 acres) of mangrove forest was lost between 2000 and 2020, according to the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organization. In Vietnam, planting of new mangroves has helped, but that progress has been undermined by losses due to aquaculture, land conversion and coastal erosion. Vietnamese officials have emphasized that the project is outside Can Gio's core, more strictly-protected area.

events.title: Asian markets dip as investors weigh tech earnings, Gulf tensions
events.summary: South Korean shares were down more than 1%. Asian shares fell as investors weighed strong tech earnings against worries about AI spending, Fed policy and Gulf tensions. Wall Street rose overnight after better results from Meta, SpaceX and Super Micro, but market focus stayed on whether AI profits can last. Safe-haven demand stayed firm: Treasury yields fell, Brent crude hit US$110.03, and US ordered diplomats out of Saudi Arabia after Houthi strikes. HONG KONG – Asian stocks struggled to stay above water in early trade on Oct 22 , as tech earnings optimism provided only fleeting support amid lingering concerns over AI and uncertainty in the Gulf . MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was down 0.2%, on track for a fourth straight week of decline. Japan’s Nikkei stock index gave up earlier gains to trade 0.4% lower, while South Korean shares were down more than 1%. US stock futures, the S&P 500 e-minis, were down 0.4% at 7,765.8. Overnight, the tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street to a higher close as better-than-expected earnings reports from market heavyweights helped ease some concerns over the sustainability and profitability of massive AI build-outs. SpaceX posted its first profit as a public company, Meta reported third-quarter revenue that beat expectations, while AI server maker Super Micro forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin that both topped estimates. However, Meta’s plan to issue non-voting Class C common stock drew renewed scrutiny on AI spending. “There’s a lot of noise out there at the moment and investors are still digesting this morning’s results,” said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com “Also, we’re really only at the start of the meaty part of earnings season, which is coming at the same time that investors are tackling the uncertainty from an upcoming Fed decision, geopolitical risks, and US mid-terms.” In a sign of subdued risk sentiment, the yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes was down 4.2 basis points at 5.1065%, while the yield on 30-year notes was at a one-week low of 5.3968%. Meanwhile, Brent crude rose 1.1% to US$110.03 a barrel, near a five-month high. The US ordered diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes, while the New York Times reported the US and Israeli militaries had developed specific plans for renewed attacks on Iran after the US midterm elections, which take place on Nov 3. In currencies, the dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of currencies of other major trading partners, dipped to 102.2. The euro was little changed at US$1.1231. The yen was also flat at 158.125, after Deputy Bank of Japan Governor Ryozo Himino signalled his readiness to raise borrowing costs. The Korean won was muted at 1325.9, after the Bank of Korea left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.00% on Oct 22 . Gold was slightly lower at US$4115.5 per ounce. Bitcoin was down 0.4% at US$84,284.05, while ether was 0.6% lower at US$2,476.34. REUTERS

events.title: No order, no seat: Starbucks China rolls out new store policy
events.summary: "Purchase to sit" signs are popping up in Starbucks stores around China Taking a seat at a Starbucks in China? Just make sure you're also ordering something there. A new policy by Starbucks China takes effect across all its 8,000 stores on Thursday, making it mandatory for people to purchase items if they want to sit in its cafes. Starbucks China said the move was part of efforts to improve the "in-store experience" for customers. The company is facing stiff competition from homegrown brands such as Luckin Coffee. Starbucks stores around the world have also been wrestling with non-paying seat-hoggers and other undesirable behaviour from customers. In South Korea, Starbucks has told customers to stop bringing "bulky items" into their stores , after some patrons reportedly hogged seats with printers and desktop computers in tow. In North America, Starbucks reversed its open-door policy which for years allowed people to use their seats and toilets without buying anything, saying that it wanted to "prioritise" paying customers. Starbucks China is now following suit. Ahead of the official announcement on Wednesday, reports of the new seating policy at China's Starbucks stores had been circulating this week - along with social media videos of what appear to be "purchase to sit" signs in Starbucks stores. Many on Chinese social media welcomed the new policy. "Finally, there won't be peak periods where people are just sitting there not ordering anything, drinking Luckin coffee, playing games and yelling on the phone," reads one of the top-liked comment on Weibo. "Every time I walk around, there's nowhere to sit," "There's nothing wrong with it. I'd feel awkward sitting there if I didn't make a purchase. I'd rather leave the seats for those who made purchases and need the seats," another Weibo user commented. Last month, a Starbucks store in Sichuan province sparked debate after video of its chained-up outdoor seats and tables were circulated on social media. It appeared to be an attempt to block people from sitting there without paying. Since opening its first store there in 1999, China has become Starbucks' second-largest market. But it has faced stiff competition in recent years from Luckin and other local brands that offer cheaper products. Luckin also offers a robust app-based ordering system that prioritises grab-and-go transactions, challenging Starbucks' model of a full cafe experience where people can sit down and enjoy their food and drinks. In 2023, Luckin overtook Starbucks as China's largest coffee chain. Starbucks said last year it would sell 60% stake of its business in China as part of a $4bn (£3.04bn) deal with investment firm Boyu Capital. In another statement on Wednesday, Starbucks China said it was planning to increase staffing and improve digital systems at its stores, among other investments to "ensure customers receive timely and warm service even during peak hours". events.title: Everyone hates Oxford Street. Will pedestrianisation save it?
events.summary: In a few days the busiest shopping street in Europe will be closed to traffic. The hope is that an unloved and polluted thoroughfare will turn into somewhere that people actually want to spend time In February, the mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, announced that Britain’s best-known thoroughfare, Oxford Street, would be pedestrianised. To the surprise of every Londoner that I have spoken to in the past few months, it is actually happening. On Monday 26 October, the busiest shopping street in Europe – or, precisely, half of its 1.2-mile stretch – will be closed to traffic, putting an end to several decades of bitter arguments, obstructions and delays. Cars, lorries, vans, taxis, buses, bicycles, ebikes, scooters will be banned. Nothing but pedestrians (and emergency vehicles) will be allowed in. This change will mark the most remarkable transformation to the streetscape of central London since at least 2003, when Trafalgar Square was turned from a glorified roundabout into one of London’s most recognisable public spaces. It will also form the most visible part of the mayor’s legacy, whether or not Khan runs for a fourth term in 2028. Three years ago, Khan published a memoir and manifesto, Breathe , attributing his asthma to growing up inhaling London’s polluted air. For the mayor, pedestrianising Oxford Street is the culmination of a mission to create a greener city that is oriented around public health, walking and cycling. Continue reading...

events.title: Mum and son offered to repay Alan Jones after being 'berated', trial hears
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts Mother of complainant was caught in 'web of dependency' with Alan Jones, court hears The mother of Complainant A is giving evidence in the Alan Jones trial on Thursday. ( ABC News: Ethan Rix ) The mother of Complainant A defends staying in contact with Alan Jones after her teenage son told her "something sexual" happened. Complainant A, who is now an adult, is alleging Mr Jones kissed him and put his hands on his bottom when he was a 17-year-old boy. Mr Jones has pleaded not guilty to 21 counts of indecent assault and sexual touching. The mother of a man who has accused Alan Jones of kissing him when he was a 17-year-old schoolboy has defended keeping in contact with the broadcaster, telling a court she was in a "web of dependency" with him. The woman has been cross-examined on day 50 of Mr Jones's criminal trial, in which Mr Jones has pleaded not guilty to 21 counts of indecent assault and sexual touching. Mr Jones is accused of kissing a 17-year-old boy, Complainant A, with his tongue and touching his bottom during a visit to his NSW Southern Highlands property. The woman told the court she offered to repay Mr Jones after feeling "berated". ( ABC News: Ethan Rix ) NSW Sexual Violence Helpline on 1800 424 017 NSW Victims Services on 1800 633 063 Bravehearts (support for child sexual abuse survivors) on 1800 272 831 Child Protection Helpline on 132 111 MARS Australia (for men affected by rape and sexual abuse) on (07) 3857 1222 National Survivors Foundation on 1300 124 433 Full Stop Australia on 1800 385 578. The NSW Local Court has heard the boy first contacted Mr Jones when he was 13 years old, asking for help for his struggling single mother, and the pair were in regular email contact while Mr Jones helped the family financially. His mother, who cannot be identified to protect the complainant, has told the court her son wrote her a note about 10 days after the alleged assault, telling her "something sexual" had happened during his visit to Mr Jones's farmstay. The court has heard the boy spoke briefly to police about the alleged assault when they turned up at his school in November of that year, but he did not want to make a complaint. Under questioning from the prosecution, the woman agreed she emailed the broadcaster that same month, seeking advice after her son had "messed up" his university application. She said Mr Jones "offered" to contact the university, and did so, but that "it came to no avail anyway" because her son's application was not accepted. "I continued to contact Mr Jones," the woman told the court. "I was in a web of dependency with Mr Jones… so a crisis would come up, and I would ask for advice." The trial has previously been told Mr Jones gave about $100,000 of his own money towards the building of the complainant and his mother's home, and used his connection to the then-head of the Commonwealth Bank to have their home loan reduced by $600,000. Emails handed up to the court show Mr Jones raised concerns with the mother and son about the "enormous cost" of his assistance. "I recall feeling berated about how much it had cost," the woman told the court. "[Complainant A and I] had a conversation to suggest that we repay money, that we go on a payment plan to pay for some of these things." The pair offered to repay Mr Jones, but he declined, the court heard. "I recall [Complainant A] and I saying to each other, 'well, we've offered… could you take us up on the offer rather than continue to berate us about your generosity?'" the woman said. Under cross-examination, Complainant A's mother was asked whether she intended to give Mr Jones the impression that emails from her son's account were coming solely from him, when in fact they were at times partly drafted by her. The mother agreed she did not specify which emails she had contributed to, but asked why anyone would expect a 14-year-old boy to know his mother's mortgage details without her input. Mr Jones's lawyers also asked why she did not produce the note her son allegedly wrote her in the aftermath of the alleged assault when her son made police statements in 2018 or 2024. The woman said she found the note in 2025, in a drawer of "stuff" in her bedroom which she had not previously searched because it was "full of emotion". Mr Jones's counsel Claire O'Neill also asked the woman whether she had "encouraged" her son to make a complaint to police, despite his reluctance to. "Did you tell him you thought it was a good idea?" Ms O'Neill asked. "I told him that I would support him in whatever he did," the woman responded.

events.title: Abu Dhabi Finance Week to make half of 2026 sessions private to drive deals
events.summary: Abu Dhabi Finance Week will hold about half of its sessions behind closed doors this year, as organisers seek to encourage more candid discussions among global financial leaders and generate tangible business outcomes. The event to be held from December 7 to 10 is expected to draw more than 40,000 attendees, including 8,000 senior executives, with financial leaders representing about $70 trillion in assets under management. Chris Hughes, editor-in-chief of ADFW, said private meetings enable senior executives to exchange information more openly than on public stages, potentially influencing investment decisions and corporate strategies. "I find that when they are in the private rooms there's a little bit more openness, a little bit more dialogue," he told ADGM's Global Media Forum on Tuesday. "It's not just monologue, it's dialogue," he added, which is physically represented by attendees and speakers alike being seated face-to-face rather than shoulder-to-shoulder. The shift towards invitation-only discussions, he said, reflects growing demand among executives for meetings that deliver practical outcomes rather than simply provide networking opportunities or public exposure. ADFW recorded 82 memorandums of understanding and partnerships in 2025, according to the organiser, Abu Dhabi’s financial centre ADGM, which was almost double the 44 agreements and announcements in 2024. The agreements involved major financial institutions and businesses including BlackRock, Franklin Templeton, Mubadala, Mastercard and Swiss Re. While the figures demonstrate the event's growing role as a platform for forging partnerships, ADGM has not disclosed how many resulted directly from private meetings or their combined monetary value. From dialogue to deals Private meetings could allow investors, regulators and executives to discuss commercially sensitive issues, identify investment opportunities and advance potential transactions without the scrutiny of a public audience. Mr Hughes referred to a closed-door leadership meeting involving the International Monetary Fund during last year's ADFW, attended by chief executives of major financial institutions. He recalled watching senior executives take handwritten notes throughout the discussions, which suggested that information exchanged in such settings could influence decisions within large organisations that aren't directly seen, but have major implications. "That extra grain of information they didn't usually have, that can change the economy of... a city or town, or company, or country, just by a tiny little 0.1 degree." The growing emphasis on private engagement comes as Abu Dhabi attracts more international financial institutions. Fourteen global financial firms managing more than $5 trillion announced plans to establish a presence in ADGM during the first half of this year, according to figures disclosed by ADGM chairman Ahmed Al Zaabi this week. ADFW is also expected to host more than 80 events and 400 content sessions this year, compared with more than 70 events and 350 sessions in 2025, according to organisers' projections. The preparations come amid regional uncertainty as the Iran war continues to disrupt business activity, energy markets and travel across the Middle East. Saudi Arabia this week postponed its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference, originally scheduled for October 26 to 29 in Riyadh, until 2027, after a series of missile and drone attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels. The attacks, including strikes on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, have raised security concerns among international executives and investors. Asked about contingency plans for ADFW amid the regional tension, Mr Hughes expressed confidence in Abu Dhabi's security and preparations to welcome international delegates in December.

events.title: Pumped hydro project scrapped after developer deems it unviable
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts Oven Mountain pumped hydro scheme abandoned by Alinta Energy Plans for a pumped hydro project in northern NSW have been scrapped. ( Supplied: Snowy Hydro ) Alinta Energy has withdrawn plans to build a $1.8 billion pumped hydro energy storage project in northern NSW. The decision comes after Origin Energy scrapped its proposed 870 megawatt Skye Ridge Wind Farm near Walcha earlier this month. Energy experts warn construction costs are rising as battery storage prices plunge, leading to once-critical stored hydro projects becoming unviable. Another large-scale renewable energy project has been scrapped, with plans for a $1.8 billion pumped hydro project in northern NSW withdrawn by the developer. The 900 megawatt Oven Mountain Pumped Hydro Energy Storage scheme was one of the largest projects within the Armidale Renewable Energy Zone. An Alinta Energy spokesperson said in a statement that "economic and timing challenges on key elements including a critical transmission line" made the project unviable. It is the second state significant renewable energy project to fail this month, after Origin Energy scrapped the proposed 870MW Skye Ridge Wind Farm near Walcha in northern NSW. Listed for consideration as a state significant development, the project was progressing through assessment phases with NSW Planning. A diagram of the proposed Oven Mountain Pumped Hydro project. ( Supplied: Oven Mountain Pumped Hydro Energy Storage Project ) "We sincerely thank traditional owners, landholders, MPs and council representatives, suppliers, key agencies and many other key stakeholders who have contributed their time, knowledge and feedback throughout the development process." A pumped hydro energy storage system works by moving water between two dams, with one at the top of a hill and another at the bottom, through a turbine. Energy stored during the day is then released during peak electricity usage at night to maximise profit. Pumped hydro moves water through a turbine. ( Supplied: Australian Renewable Energy Agency ) The Oven Mountain project was planned for a site near Georges Junction at the rural hamlet of Carrai, 60 kilometres south-east of Armidale and 75 kilometres north-west of Kempsey. When it was first announced, it was identified as being critical to state infrastructure. Armidale Shire Mayor Sam Coupland said the decision to scrap the project had left him in shock, with the council only finding out about the decision this morning. Cr Coupland questioned whether state and federal planning regulations had become too onerous. Sam Coupland says he was shocked to learn about the project's cancellation. ( ABC News: James Paras ) "It seems there are too many environmental hoops to jump through," he said. "That seems to be killing important projects, whether it's this, other renewable energy projects [or] inland rail, take your pick. "There just seems to be too many hurdles to get through that are imposing a cost that makes these things unviable." Cr Coupland said the council had worked with developer Alinta Energy for several years to plan roadworks to support the project. "That Kempsey-to-Armidale Road restoration project is the biggest engineering undertaken by any council ever in NSW," he said. Michael Kemp says the Oven Mountain project cancellation is a poor economic result for the community. ( ABC Coffs Coast: Claire Simmonds ) The state member for the coastal electorate of Oxley, Michael Kemp, said the decision was a "poor result for the community". "It's a loss for the community on the mid north coast," he said. "This project would have provided significant trades jobs, not only during the construction, but ongoing." The site location is in the steep, forested country of the Great Dividing Range and home to Thunggutti Indigenous people. Arthur Bain says reaction to the project cancellation will be mixed. ( Supplied ) Kempsey deputy mayor and Thunggutti Local Aboriginal Land Council chief executive Arthur Bain said there would be mixed feelings about the loss of the project. "If we think about the site of Oven Mountain, it's perfect for pumped hydro because it is very steep gorge country and it's got the natural falls to generate the electricity," he said. "On the other hand, its location also makes it unviable economically because it is so isolated." Cr Bain said a previous hydro project proposed for the site failed in the 1980s. "You've really got to go out there and put your boots on the ground and see what that country was like. [It's hard] to imagine just getting machinery out there," he said.

( ABC News: Keana Naughton ) Entire teams of National Australia Bank workers are having to reapply for their jobs and compete among themselves as part of a major restructure. Staff say the writing was on the wall as they witnessed the bank pushing to offshore workers and take up AI. The major bank revealed plans to slash 2,500 roles by June next year, with 1,500 expected to be out the door before Christmas. National Australia Bank (NAB) workers have accused the banking giant of a "spill and fill" redundancy strategy, forcing entire teams to reapply for their positions as part of a sweeping restructure. Earlier this week the major bank revealed plans to slash 2,500 roles by June , including 1,500 before Christmas. This is about 6 per cent of its total workforce, with corporate roles bearing the brunt. Several workers who spoke to the ABC on condition of anonymity said the writing was on the wall as the bank pushed the uptake of AI and moved work offshore. "Until today, it's been a lovely place to work," said Dylan*, who has worked in NAB's technology team for a decade but learnt he could be unemployed by the end of the year. His team will have to reapply for their jobs in what is known as a "spill and fill" type of workforce restructure, where existing roles are made vacant and current employees have to fight for a smaller number of positions. There is a two-week consultation period for Dylan's team and, for those being shown the door, their last day will be December 2 or 17. Do you know more about this or have a similar story? Email turner-cohen.alex@abc.net.au Andrew Irvine says the changes are "expected to improve outcomes for customers". ( AAP: Mick Tsikas ) NAB chief executive Andrew Irvine said in a note to staff he encouraged colleagues to be "thoughtful" and check in on one another, and indicated support would be offered to those "impacted personally". The bank said in an ASX announcement that the mass redundancies, which are estimated to cost the bank about $300 million in restructuring costs, were part of "actions to simplify its operating model and better align its workforce to prioritise growth and technology initiatives for customers". The bank declined to comment to the ABC on staff members' claims. The looming redundancies have sparked serious concerns about offshoring among staff, as the banking heavyweight bolsters its Indian and Vietnamese headcount while it cuts staff based in Australia. A leaked workforce plan seen by the ABC shows Dylan's team in technology, which consists of just under 500 people, is currently 53 per cent Australian-based. The rest are based in NAB's offices in India (14 per cent), Vietnam (13 per cent), or are external contractors. But, under the plan, the number of staff would be reduced to 400 by the 2027 financial year while the percentage of offshore workers would increase. The Australian-based workforce would be cut to 40 per cent, with the Indian and Vietnamese offices upping their numbers to 30 and 20 per cent respectively. NAB announced mass redundancies on Tuesday. ( ABC News: Yiying Li ) James* resigned last Friday, just days before NAB announced it was going to slash staff, because of fears about the longevity of his business banking role. He shared an email NAB sent in March, which stated the bank would be "expanding out teams in NAB India" to help in its goal of "focusing on digitising and simplifying processes, including increasing automation to speed up turnaround time" and "investing in our global teams". James said the messaging in NAB had changed so drastically in the past six months that he no longer felt safe in his job and had left the banking industry. "People are feeling the anxiety," he said, adding that he had moved to a service-based industry because, "I can't be replaced realistically for the next five to 10 years." AI is also an issue on everyone's lips. While there was no direct reference to AI, NAB did refer to "rapid technological change" in its announcement to the market and experts say its impact is clear. events.title: The 'trillion pound' oil fund the government believes Britain could have built
events.summary: The Jackdaw gas platform and drilling rig in the North Sea. After a half-century wait, the United Kingdom now has an oil fund. Chancellor John Healey announced the creation of an Energy Wealth Fund at the Jackdaw gas approval announcement on Wednesday, with £2bn of funding housed in the National Wealth Fund. A selection of energy exporting countries, mainly in the Gulf, but also including Norway, over the years have amassed multi-trillion funds using oil and gas revenues to create epic national piggy banks. It has been a long-standing debate in UK economic policy circles. If neighbouring Norway has amassed a $2.4tn war chest from the same North Sea, where exactly did the UK's sovereign wealth fund go? It is an apposite question on the week when the national debt also hit £3tn for the first time. "The proceeds of this oil and gas coming ashore now can be invested for the future generations," the chancellor said. "If we had done this when North Sea oil was first discovered in the 1980s, we'd have a British Sovereign Wealth Fund now that would be worth probably a trillion pounds." On Wednesday, for the first time, Treasury officials actually calculated how much that missing British fund could have been worth. The trillion pound number comes from internal Treasury modelling. The assumption was that the UK's historical North Sea receipts of £200bn had been invested, with no withdrawals and grown at a rate comparable to Norway's. "Norway demonstrates the power of long-term investment: the government wants to learn from that principle, rather than copy its model wholesale," one insider told me. It was a "missed opportunity" which "had we systematically invested those receipts, we could have built a huge national asset for future generations", they said. Burnham defends Jackdaw decision as Badenoch urges PM to overturn ban on new oil and gas licences Published 1 day ago It is a giant "What if?" asked often by economists critical of the Margaret Thatcher era. The peak oil revenues were, in their view, frittered away in pre-election tax cuts, which ended up being spent on 1980s garden conservatories. Others might argue that the revenues under subsequent governments were squandered on wasteful government spending. It is worth noting that Norway's fund only began in earnest in 1996. The idea of a lost oil fund has also featured in arguments from supporters of Scottish independence, and was suggested by some government advisers in the 1970s. I have met some of the officials running Norway's fund. They are sometimes lambasted by ordinary Norwegians on the Oslo commuter trains who can all check the live value of the national fund. Three percent of its value is drawn down each year to fund a fifth to a quarter of government budgets. The nation drew down on the fund during the coronavirus pandemic. It is meant to help fund Norway's post oil economy and society, as indeed are some of the equivalent funds in the Gulf. It is a gift to the future. While the UK government promises to divert new revenues into its new fund, it will be run rather differently. Norway's fund is obliged to invest abroad, and has grown hugely off the back off investments in US big tech. The UK plan is to create a fund that can invest domestically in green energy. It may struggle to match the performance. UK energy tax revenues are also forecast to dwindle as North Sea production slows. The rate of slowing may now ease, with Jackdaw and extensions to existing fields. Critically Norway's state still controls its oil companies, also giving a share of their profits. Two billion Norwegian Kroner was exactly the starting investment in Norway's fund 30 years ago. It is now worth over a thousand times that. Nobody expects the Energy Wealth Fund's £2bn to be worth £2tn by 2056. The question is, what might have been, had a similar, far-sighted idea been adopted here in decades past? How much gas could Jackdaw provide? And will it cut your energy bills? events.title: Democrats accuse Trump of using prosecution threats to pressure election officials
events.summary: Democratic groups sued the Trump administration Tuesday, accusing it of using unfounded voter fraud claims to muscle its way into how states run elections. Why it matters: The groups say the administration is issuing a stream of threats to intimidate and bully both voters and election officials. They're asking a judge to declare the administration's actions unlawful and block further interference. Driving the news: The lawsuit condemns the administration for targeting state voter rolls by insisting that local officials review federally compiled lists of alleged noncitizens on their voter rolls. The suit also alleges that the administration is improperly demanding that states deny ballots to registered voters based on those federal lists. The Democrat-aligned groups also claim the administration has attempted to intimidate state and local officials by threatening them with jail time or prosecution. Case in point: The lawsuit cites a Department of Homeland Security claim that Nevada had nearly 16,000 noncitizens on its voter rolls. The department later claimed that it had confirmed 185 of those people were noncitizens. State records later indicated that all 185 were citizens. The DOJ also demanded that California deny ballots to more than 20,000 people based on a federal list that flagged them as suspected ineligible voters, the lawsuit says. A preliminary investigation by Los Angeles County investigators found that more than 25% of those flagged listed a U.S. birthplace, and others already had their voter registrations canceled. What they're saying: "Department of Justice and DHS officials have sought to bolster their interference efforts through a persistent stream of threats and intimidation directed towards state and local election officials across the country," the groups' attorneys wrote. "Defendants' coercive threats of legal retaliation against state officials, including even potential imprisonment, for simply following state law and aiding registered voters in casting their ballots objectively intimidate voters and election officials alike, in violation of Section 11(b) of the Voting Rights Act." The suit, brought by Democratic organizations including the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, Democratic leaders and a voter, names Trump, the Departments of Justice and Homeland Security, and their respective heads as defendants. The other side: "The Justice Department enforces federal election law, and election integrity is a top priority," a DOJ spokesperson told Axios. "Every action the Department has taken to protect the integrity of this year's elections is grounded in the law and being litigated in open court. Ensuring that only eligible citizens vote and that every lawful ballot is counted is a requirement of federal law," according to the emailed statement. "We notified California that noncitizens are likely registered to vote, and we asked the state to independently verify the citizenship of any ballots cast by people on a list that we provided. It refused to do so. Federal law doesn't permit this willful blindness." A White House spokesperson told Axios that while "Democrats and the media continue to dismiss concerns about voter fraud, the Trump Administration is taking decisive lawful action to protect our elections including prosecuting election crimes, strengthening election infrastructure security, and protecting vulnerable voters from fraud and coercion." A spokesperson for Homeland Security told Axios that the department's "message to aliens who vote in American elections is clear: we will find you, arrest you, and you will face the consequences — including criminal charges and deportation." Zoom out: The suit also argues that the president has no constitutional authority to decide who gets to vote or dictate how states count ballots. Investigations and audits have found no evidence of widespread voter fraud. Research shows noncitizen voting is rare, and there's no evidence it occurs on a scale that could swing elections. Go deeper: Trump sues California to prevent counting 20,000 voters' ballots Editor's note: This story has been updated with comment from the White House and DHS.

events.title: The grads ditching the UK for a fresh start abroad
events.summary: Charlie West, left, Rachel James and Owein Iveson have all moved overseas Last year Rachel James quit her corporate job in London, packed a suitcase and booked a one-way ticket to Sydney, without a job lined up or a plan in place. "I went for a fresh start," says the 26-year-old from Surrey. "To take a risk and try something completely different. With the worst case being there will always be a flight home if all fails." More than one in 10 UK university students are now planning to move abroad for better opportunities after they have graduated, up from 7.8% two years ago, according to a survey , external of 15,000 final year university students. Meanwhile, a study by the Institute of Student Employers (ISE) says that competition for graduate jobs in the UK was at a three-decade high. UK employers now receive 140 applications per graduate vacancy on average, an increase of 14% from 2025, and up from just 30 applications per vacancy 20 years ago, according to the ISE's report , external . For young British adults going abroad, where are they heading? Australia: 'The weather's beautiful, even in the winter' While there is no age-specific data for which countries people go to, Australia remains by far the most popular nation for British adults overall who move abroad, official figures show. , external In addition to Australia's weather and use of the English language, another reason is its visa-friendly policy. Under its Working Holiday Maker programme, , external British passport holders between the ages of 18 and 35 can live in Australia for up to three years. Rachel James says that Sydney is a nicer place to live and work than London Rachel, who graduated from Loughborough University in 2022 with a degree in English, had been working for accountancy giant PricewaterhouseCoopers in the UK. She now has a job in marketing in Sydney for gym chain Fitness First. She says her annual salary has gone down from £42,000 to £37,000, while she now pays $AUS 2,000 (£1,000) a month to rent a two-bedroom apartment with a friend, similar to what she was paying in London. Despite having less disposable income, she has no regrets. "The weather's beautiful, even in the winter, and the walks on my doorstep are unmatched. "People want to leave work at 5pm so they can go and do their hobbies - whether it's surfing, running, enjoying the sunset, a picnic or sunset yoga. I didn't come with career progression as a focus - it's more about the different way of life." Around two-thirds of British nationals who emigrate are aged between 16 and 34, according to the most recent figures , external from the UK's Office for National Statistics. It said that 75,000 more people in that age bracket left the UK in 2025 than arrived. After Australia the next most popular destination for British adults is the US. Charlie West says that working in the US has given him better pay and more opportunities Charlie West, 25, from Cheshire, moved to the States in 2024 for better pay and opportunities in academia after he completed a masters in medieval studies at Oxford University. West is now two years in to a six-year funded PhD course at Yale's Department of Italian Studies, which includes him teaching. "I really wanted to do a PhD but it's difficult to get funding in the UK, particularly in the humanities, and funded stipends are about £21,000. I'd have had to work [outside academia] at the same time to afford to live. "In the US I'm paid $51,000 a year (£37,770), about to rise to $52,000, and it comes with a lot more opportunities to teach and travel to conferences." Europe: 'If you can work across the EU there are more opportunities' The European Union also remains popular with young Britons looking to move abroad, although the visa requirements since Brexit have made it more difficult. One way to get into the European jobs market is to have studied in the EU. International graduates can apply for a permanent residence permit after their degree ends. Owein Iveson has no plans to return to the UK from Finland This is what Owein Iveson, 24, from Sunderland, is doing as he is about to graduate from Finland's Aalto University with a masters in design. Owein says he "fell in love with the country" after visiting for the first time in 2020. "Finland's a beautiful country," he says. "The streets are very clean. It's a very quiet lifestyle. The nature is fantastic and the public transport works really efficiently." Owein lives in Espoo, a city about 15 minutes on the metro from Helsinki, and doesn't expect to return to the UK anytime soon. "To be honest the jobs market is not great in Finland, but there is high demand for IT workers, and if you can work across the EU there are many more opportunities." Immigration lawyer John Kiely, a London-based partner at international law firm Howard Kennedy, says it is easy to see why more UK graduates are looking overseas.

events.title: Scoop: Dems quietly guide super PACs to boost spoiler House candidates
events.summary: House Democrats' campaign arm is instructing allied super PACs to promote minor candidates in several key House races, Axios has learned. Why it matters: This allows Democrats to steer outside groups toward siphoning votes from Republicans without violating laws against direct coordination. An Axios review of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee's "redboxes" — publicly available webpages laying out what PACs should say in ads and which voters to target — found references to minor candidates in five races. The DCCC included language on four of those pages promoting a third-party or independent candidate with language touting their conservative, pro-gun or anti-government bona fides. "Registered Republicans under the age of 55 need to see ads," the redbox for Colorado's 5th District says, "showing that ... Christopher Mitchell, a libertarian, is the true conservative running for Congress." The page for Virginia's 2nd District says white, college-educated men should see that independent J. Matt Baker is "a staunch supporter of the 2nd amendment" who will "defend our constitution." In Virginia's 5th District , the DCCC wants the same group of voters to know that independent Cooke Harvey "will fight for Virginia's farmers against big government." Republican women in Nevada's 2nd District should be informed that American Independent Party candidate Lynn Chapman "has spent decades fighting for conservative values," the DCCC says. Zoom in: In several cases, the redboxes urge super PACs to steer Democratic and left-leaning voters away from minor candidates who could siphon votes from the DCCC's recruit. The redbox for Alaska's at-large district — where Democrats are backing independent Bill Hill — says voters need to know Eric Hafner is a "fake Democrat" despite being listed on the ballot as one, noting he is an inmate in New York with no clear ties to Alaska . The page for Virginia's 2nd District urges PACs to ding the progressive credentials of another independent candidate, Geral D. "Bishop" Staten , a self-identified "Democrat Socialist." Black voters should hear that Staten "said that he would vote for Donald Trump in 2024 and said that President Obama is a quote 'puppet and a clown,'" the DCCC redbox says — though he has denied supporting Trump. Between the lines: In the post-Citizens United era, redboxes have emerged as a way for campaigns to give messaging guidance to cash-rich outside groups that often have less localized knowledge of their turf. The practice is so named because the websites often put a red box around the instructions. The NRCC has its own publicly available redboxes , though it shies away from encouraging PACs to boost spoiler candidates. The big picture: There have been several other isolated examples this year of both parties allegedly boosting spoiler candidates, including with redboxes. Democrats successfully sued last month to get a Green Party candidate who they alleged was a GOP plant booted off the ballot in Pennsylvania's 7th District. Republicans in Alaska tried and failed to do the same with unaffiliated candidate Dan J. Sullivan, who they allege is a spoiler for Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan in his race against Democrat Mary Peltola. It's even happened in party primaries: The campaign of Rep. Doris Matsui (D-Calif.) put language on its redbox promoting Republican Zachariah Wooden in the hopes of keeping progressive challenger Mai Vang out of the general election.
