events.title: Whoop sees Abu Dhabi as springboard for shift to predictive health, says chief executive
events.summary: Whoop is pushing deeper into the Gulf's longevity economy. The Boston-based human performance company this week announced a clinical research partnership with Abu Dhabi's Department of Health. The deal builds on a $75 million anchor investment from Mubadala Investment Company and a broader buildout that has made the GCC one of Whoop's fastest-growing markets . “This region has become one of the most important regions for Whoop,” its founder and chief executive Will Ahmed tells On the Record with Hadley Gamble . “We're growing extraordinarily fast here in the GCC. We're up about 15 times in the last three years. Our membership base here has grown over 85 per cent just in the past year.” The company has separately put GCC year-on-year growth at more than 75 per cent. Speaking on stage at the Abu Dhabi Future Health Summit , Mr Ahmed said the Department of Health agreement would fund “powerful clinical research to drive health outcomes” around prevention, sleep, cardiovascular health and ageing. The announcement is the latest layer in a multiyear capital and operational push by Abu Dhabi entities into Whoop, which produces wearable health trackers. On May 7, Whoop and Mubadala said they had formed a strategic partnership “to advance proactive health, performance science and preventative healthcare innovation in the UAE”, anchored by the $75 million investment. That investment was made as part of Whoop's $575 million Series G, which valued the company at $10.1 billion. The round was led by Collaborative Fund and, according to the company, included Mubadala and Abu Dhabi-based 2PointZero Group. Under terms disclosed by both sides, Whoop would establish a dedicated office in Abu Dhabi , expand its Advanced Labs blood-testing product, introduce full Arabic localisation across its platform – launched this month with a GCC-wide campaign – and launch the Whoop-Mubadala Health Research Initiative, a longitudinal research programme aimed at strengthening the UAE's health value chain from diagnostics and genomics to prevention and behavioural optimisation. Mr Ahmed has cast the UAE capital as a proving ground for a shift from reactive to predictive care. “The power of continuous health monitoring is that it can really understand signals in your body that you may not be able to feel,” he says. “We believe those insights can actually drive health outcomes, which is to say it can make you lower your weight, it can make you decrease your blood pressure.” He says the company's thesis since its launch 14 years ago – to validate continuous monitoring with elite athletes and then move into the mainstream – is now playing out in the Gulf. He acknowledges the timing, closing a large Gulf investment shortly after the Iran war began, reflects a long-term commitment. “The timing of some of that partnership was complicated with the wars in this region. But to me, it was obvious to show up because I'd been showing up for the last decade,” he says. For Abu Dhabi, the Whoop partnership is one piece of a broader longevity infrastructure play. An EY survey cited by Abu Dhabi officials found only 43 per cent of respondents follow a structured fitness plan, even as 61 per cent had used a wearable in the past year and 87 per cent reported a positive experience using AI for health decisions – a gap officials believe wearables plus clinical integration can close. Whoop, which has now raised about $1 billion in total capital, said the Gulf expansion would be paired with retail distribution, sponsorships with the UAE Team Emirates-XRG cyclists and Al Nassr football team, and, through Whoop Qatar, its first performance research and developement lab outside Boston, later in 2026. “There are many countries in the world that are excited about wearable technology,” Mr Ahmed says. “When you can remove bureaucracy and you can say, look, no, we want health care not to be reactive but actually proactive, then a lot of things fall in suit.”

events.title: Breach of Paris Agreement global warming level ‘inevitable,’ UN says
events.summary: Efforts to cap global temperature rises have largely failed and a breach of the Paris Agreement’s limit of 1.5℃ is now “inevitable,” the UN said. Overall global warming is now likely to be between 2.6℃ and 2.8℃ by the end of the century, the UN Environment Programme predicted. It warned that the best-case scenario — in which humanity overshoots its target but ultimately reverts to it — would require cuts to global emissions of about 45% by 2035; current national plans, even if fully implemented, would only lead to reductions of up to 15% . Yet, UNEP argued, “countries can still limit peak warming, shorten the duration of overshoot, and keep the goals of the Paris Agreement within reach.” — Prashant Rao

events.title: Bringing the Spark to Europe: Local Intelligence Powers Next Wave of Agents
events.summary: At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is showcasing its full lineup of local AI hardware. RTX Spark , which launched last week , powers personal agents on Windows PCs; DGX Spark supports developers building and scaling applications on Linux; and DGX Station serves enterprise teams running frontier workloads on Linux, with a Windows version arriving in December. Underdog Desktop Agent now available for RTX Spark DGX Spark 64GB available on Friday, Oct. 23 NVIDIA Sync to support eight DGX Sparks and add Model Launcher this month October DGX Spark software update adds Wi-Fi Assistant and updates DGX Spark Skills DGX Station improves manageability with seven new integrations DGX Station for Windows launches in December with support for many manufacturing apps and agent harnesses Three new open source reference workflows for robotics on DGX Station NVIDIA Cloud Functions is coming in early access to DGX Station Recursive Flint, a new local coding model, is now available for NVIDIA local hardware Day-0 support for new Nemotron, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, MiniMax and FLUX.3 AI models New accelerations for llama.cpp and vLLM inference engines and a new collection of checkpoints optimized for local AI hardware. Learn more about these local AI announcements below, and check out the demos and sessions at GTC Berlin . RTX Spark Brings Personal Agents to the Windows PC RTX Spark is a new beginning for the PC — running personal agents, accelerated content creation and 1440p 100 frames-per-second gaming with up to 128GB of unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute. Here’s what early reviewers are saying about the platform since its October 16 release: “A dream machine for serious creators … ” — CGMag “Designed for the future of AI … ” — The Verge “An extremely capable, surprisingly portable and efficient machine … ” — PCMag Underdog , a new desktop agent app built for fully local, private AI, is also bringing its experience to RTX Spark. Powered by its Husky model-specific inference engine, Underdog runs models entirely on device, so personal agents can get work done without user data ever leaving the PC. Underdog is available now for download . To better enable developers and enthusiasts to build and customize local agents, many RTX Spark laptops come with an unlocked bootloader. During the GTC keynote, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang showed off how AI agents running on RTX Spark can be used to train Hugging Face’s Microduck robot using NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Hermes Agent and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B. ASUS , Dell Technologies , HP , Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI laptops are available today, with Acer coming soon. Learn more about RTX Spark , and get started with the latest RTX Spark playbooks . DGX Spark Gives Developers Room to Build New DGX Spark 64GB systems — that can run models including Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B 24GB, Qwen3.8 27B and Gemma 4 26B-A4B — start rolling out from partners on Friday, Oct. 23. When workloads require more capacity, developers can connect multiple DGX Spark systems via built-in NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking and NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant . This allows users to run advanced coding models like Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, DeepSeek v4 Flash 0731 and GLM 5.3 Flash. Now, DGX Spark supports clusters of up to eight units in manual configuration, enabling larger models, longer contexts, concurrent agents and distributed development. Ideal for small teams sharing a single cluster as a backend, with each developer running concurrent sessions against the same model, it delivers 1TB of unified memory — enough to run frontier-class models like GLM 5.3. Get started with the DGX Spark cluster playbook . NVIDIA Sync Model Launcher will also be available later this month. It simplifies access to local AI on a single DGX Spark or a cluster. With a few clicks, Model Launcher downloads a model and container suited to the configuration and connects the model to OpenCode. It automatically loads DGX Spark Skills for troubleshooting, device maintenance, access to official documentation and other workflow guidance. The October DGX Spark software update brings a new Wi-Fi Assistant that lets users switch networks when DGX Spark is running in appliance mode. Plus, DGX Spark Skills provide workflow-focused guidance in troubleshooting and device maintenance directly into NVIDIA Sync via OpenCode. DGX Spark systems are available directly from Acer , ASUS , Dell Technologies , GIGABYTE , HP , Lenovo, MSI and NVIDIA. DGX Station Puts Frontier Intelligence at the Desk For larger teams, DGX Station offers 748GB of coherent memory and up to 20 petaflops of AI performance, enabling developers to run advanced models like GLM 5.3 and serve 30+ users at speeds comparable to those provided by cloud models. Adding scale, NVIDIA Sync now supports DGX Station, simplifying connections between two Linux-based systems. New integrations with Absolute Security , Splunk by Cisco , Fleet Device Managemen t , Microsoft Intune , Perforce Puppet , Progress Software Chef and Tanium let IT teams manage DGX Station systems through enterprise setup, management and conformity processes, helping accelerate approvals and reduce deployment risk while minimizing time to first token. With the upcoming Windows-based systems, developers can build workflows that harness professional applications, run on NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs and operate from agents that run their large language models (LLMs) on NVIDIA GB300 systems — all in one machine. DGX Station for Windows , expected from system manufacturer partners in December, extends local AI into the applications and operating environment enterprises already use. Engineers can run local models and agents in Windows-native software with access to AI models, tools and agents on the same system. DGX Station for Windows will feature support for manufacturing applications from nTop , Dassault Systèmes , Keysight Technologies , MathWorks , Rockwell Automation , Siemens , Synopsys , Unity and Altera for AI-guided design, simulation, validation and engineering automation. Users will be able to run agents using Hermes Agent , Perplexity or Aible on premises for agentic control in enterprise environments. The same local, controlled computing model extends to robotics. DGX Station gives robotics teams dedicated compute for post-training, simulation and evaluation, shortening iteration cycles without waiting for shared infrastructure. NVIDIA released three open source reference workflows that bring GPT-6 Astra, NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Isaac Lab-Arena and Cosmos to NVIDIA DGX Station. Developers can use them to refine GR00T 1.7 models with reinforcement learning, train dexterous manipulation skills and post-train Cosmos world models for synthetic data generation. NVIDIA Cloud Functions is coming in early access to Linux-based DGX Station. Teams can register local model endpoints in a shared catalog and access them through one OpenAI-compatible entry point.

events.title: Google Cloud and NVIDIA Announce General Availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Infrastructure
events.summary: General availability of the instances is coming next month, with planned expansion of availability to Europe — bringing an integrated platform for training, inference and large-scale reinforcement learning to cloud customers. A5X instances bring together NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud Virgo Network and Google Cloud’s fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology for demanding agentic inference and reinforcement learning workloads at scale. Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to as many as 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multiple sites. Ineffable Intelligence , a London-based technology company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, was the first customer to access A5X. Ineffable is using the platform to advance large-scale reinforcement learning and shape “superlearner” systems that learn continuously from experience. Learning through interaction requires a continuous cycle of generating experience, evaluating outcomes and updating models, requiring infrastructure that can support the entire process at scale. A5X brings Vera Rubin into Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer as an integrated system, combining compute, networking and storage to support experience-driven learning at scale. “We’re building superlearners that continually improve through their own experience,” said David Silver, founder and CEO of Ineffable Intelligence. “That demands both substantial compute and a tight connection between generating experience and training on it, so each improvement in the agent can quickly shape its next experience. Vera Rubin’s combination of compute performance and high-bandwidth connectivity, between the Vera CPU and Rubin GPUs and between the Rubin GPUs within the rack, allow us to push the scale and ambition of our reinforcement learning research further.” WPP , a London-based marketing and communications company, has also demonstrated its creative agent reference architecture on NVIDIA Vera Rubin-based A5X instances using NVIDIA Nemotron models and NVIDIA OpenShell, part of the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for safe AI agents. The agents turn conversational requests into multistep creative workflows, such as video generation, upscaling and restyling, with human approval before execution. OpenShell provides governed sandboxes for agent execution, helping control access to sensitive brand assets and creative tools. In WPP’s initial tests, workloads that typically required a multi-node cluster ran on a single A5X instance. As organizations deploy agentic systems, they need to protect the proprietary models and sensitive data that power these systems — even when running on infrastructure they don’t own. Google Cloud will be among the first cloud providers to offer NVIDIA Confidential Computing at rack scale on bare metal instances such as A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72. Additionally, Google Cloud is making Confidential Computing generally available on G4 VMs powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, offering a flexible platform for confidential inference and fine-tuning. Customers including Vertebrae , Polaris Cloud and Confidential Core AI are using Confidential G4 for conversational privacy, verifiable agent execution and policy-governed enterprise intelligence. To support energy-efficient deployment at scale, Google Cloud and NVIDIA are exploring NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS capabilities for Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to help optimize performance per watt and expand capacity within available data-center power budgets. Learn more about NVIDIA Vera Rubin and Google Cloud A5X instances. events.title: Former chief executive banned after misconduct led to £4m losses in high-risk investments
events.summary: The FCA has banned Jeffrey Dawkins, the former chief executive of Vector Wealth Ltd, after he dishonestly acted as a front for a disqualified director using the company to sell high-risk bonds. Mr Dawkins has also been fined nearly £270,000.In 2019, Mr Dawkins sold Vector Wealth to a disqualified director who described himself as CEO and wanted to use Vector Wealth’s FCA-authorised status to sell mini-bonds.Mr Dawkins told the FCA he was still in charge, but the new “CEO” was really running the firm. This deception allowed the disqualified director to promote mini-bonds using the legitimacy of the firm to make them appear safer than they were.The disqualified director and Kadir Kanizi, a former senior manager at Vector Wealth, promoted the bonds but investors were not properly warned about the risks.Investors put in £105,000 on average, with one investing £1.1 million. Before seeing the marketing material, they had to confirm they were high net worth or sophisticated investors. Investors are expected to lose about £4 million.The FCA has banned Mr Kanizi from senior management roles. He was fined for failing to make sure consumers were properly warned about the risks.Therese Chambers, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA, said, 'Jeffrey Dawkins acted as a front man for a banned director, helping high-risk investments look safer than they were.'Mr Dawkins and Mr Kanizi allowed misleading promotions to draw in investors, many of whom now face significant losses. Mini-bonds and similar investments are very high risk, and people should be extremely cautious.'The FCA has warned about the risks of investing in mini-bonds and loan notes. A loan note or mini-bond usually involves lending money to a company for a set period in return for interest. If that company fails, consumers could lose every penny.Consumers need to be alert to the risk of harm and protect themselves using the tools available, like the FCA Firm Checker.Notes to editorsRead the final notices for Jeffrey Dawkins and Kadir Kanizi.There is statutory obligation to report the change in control of authorised firms.Vector Wealth Limited was formed as Fifth Quarter Asset Management (UK) Limited on 23 March 2012. Mr Dawkins held authorised positions at the firm from 5 March 2013. Vector Wealth’s authorisation ended on 28 January 2025.Mr Kanizi was appointed as a director on 22 September 2020 and was approved by the FCA on 6 September 2021.The disqualified director was banned from acting as a company director for 12 years in August 2014.The penalty in respect of Mr Dawkins includes a multiplier to reflect the seriousness of the conduct. It also includes an uplift for failing to cooperate with the FCA’s investigation. The full calculation is set out at section 6 of the Final Notice. Mr Dawkins has also been ordered to pay £57,298 plus interest (£68,257) of the proceeds he received from selling Vector Wealth and continuing to act as its director and approved person.The FCA has calculated that Kadir Kanizi should have been fined £80,096 but it reduced the penalty to £20,000 after he demonstrated that it would cause serious financial hardship. In the interest of maximising the funds available to be distributed to investors, the FCA agreed not to enforce the penalty if the same amount was made available by Mr Kanizi to Vector Wealth’s liquidators. He has also agreed to complete consumer duty training before taking up any future role in financial services.Investors who bought bonds through Vector Wealth should contact the firm’s liquidator and check the FCA website for updates.The FCA has investigated the matters that fall within its remit. The FCA may share relevant information with other law enforcement agencies where appropriate. Confirming or comment on individual referrals could risk affecting ongoing investigations.The FCA now actively removes the unutilised permissions of firms. Historically firms were expected to voluntarily request cancellation of unused permissions.The FCA permanently banned the marketing of speculative illiquid securities, including mini-bonds and loan notes, to retail investors from 1 January 2021.Anyone approached about loan notes, mini-bonds or similar high-risk investments should stop and check before investing, especially where adverts promise big, fixed returns or make the investment look simple and safe. Use the FCA’s Firm Checker and Warning List before handing over any money.

events.title: NVIDIA and Supply Chain Partners Expand Capacity to Accelerate AI Infrastructure Buildout
events.summary: Substrate agreements with IBIDEN, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Unimicron Technology Corporation will, in aggregate, drive a 2.5x increase in capacity over the next three years. Amkor plans to increase its advanced packaging capacity by more than 300% by the end of 2028. KYEC will build new facilities in the U.S., supported by a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance from NVIDIA. SPIL is targeting to increase its optical-engine capacity for co-packaged optics by 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028. GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced plans with a group of supply chain partners to expand global manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand for its accelerated computing and full-stack AI factory platform. Working with Amkor Technology, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and Unimicron Technology Corporation, NVIDIA is enabling new and existing suppliers to expand critical manufacturing capabilities across substrates, advanced packaging, testing and optical engines, strengthening the resiliency and redundancy of NVIDIA’s global supply chain. “We are in the midst of the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Demand is extraordinary. Capacity is the constraint,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Our supply chain partners are the world’s best manufacturers. I’m grateful they are expanding capacity around the globe to scale production and help us deliver the AI supercomputing systems powering this new industrial revolution.” Expanding Substrate Capacity to Support Volume Growth NVIDIA plans to increase substrate capacity for its products by 2.5x over the next three years. The agreements below will contribute to this capacity expansion, with more underway. Under an agreement signed and announced earlier this year by IBIDEN, NVIDIA is providing a multibillion-dollar capacity reservation advance to support IBIDEN’s Ono Plant in Japan. The expansion targets capacity reaching 3x current levels at the plant, with additional capacity expected to begin ramping in the first quarter of 2028. Samsung Electro-Mechanics is joining NVIDIA’s substrate supply chain, bringing immediate capacity from its existing operations in South Korea. The collaboration also supports facility upgrades and new factories in Sejong and Busan, South Korea. By 2028, production allocated to NVIDIA is projected to account for a significant portion of Samsung Electro-Mechanics’ total annual package substrate production capacity. NVIDIA is supporting Unimicron’s KF substrate manufacturing expansion in Taiwan with a capacity reservation agreement. The expansion is expected to begin adding capacity in the second quarter of 2027 and reach full capacity by mid-2028. Scaling Advanced Packaging for Next-Generation Platforms NVIDIA and Amkor plan to expand advanced packaging capacity in South Korea, targeting a greater than 300% increase in interposer wafer capacity by the end of 2028. The planned capacity expansion, alongside Amkor’s development of new manufacturing facilities in South Korea, will support higher production volumes for NVIDIA’s current and next-generation platforms. Expanding Semiconductor Testing and Strengthening US Manufacturing NVIDIA expects its total semiconductor testing capacity to double from calendar 2026 to 2027, supported by buildouts in the U.S., Taiwan and Singapore. NVIDIA’s $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance to KYEC will support new U.S. testing facilities and equipment, with high-volume production targeted for April 2027. In Singapore, expanded testing operations are expected to begin high-volume production in February 2027. Creating the Infrastructure for Co-Packaged Optics NVIDIA and SPIL plan to expand manufacturing capacity in Taiwan for optical engines used in co-packaged optics, supporting the growing connectivity requirements of large-scale computing infrastructure. The expansion targets an increase of 15x by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028. About NVIDIA NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) is the world leader in AI and accelerated computing. events.title: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents
events.summary: Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements. In tests using NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, Nscale demonstrated that NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS enabled 37% more GPUs and nearly 50% higher aggregate inference throughput within the same provisioned power budget. Nscale also plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure for frontier-model training and production workloads to support leading model and application builders using its full-stack, vertically integrated platform with expansion across five European markets. Crusoe is developing Spark, its liquid-cooled modular AI factories designed for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, to bring Crusoe Cloud capacity closer to users for low-latency AI inference. Crusoe Cloud serves leading model and application builders across EMEA, including Base44, Gradium, LTX and Wonderful. Aleria, Cassava Technologies , Firebird , G42 , Radiant, SWI Compute and Vultr are also developing and expanding NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure across Europe, the Nordics, Africa and Central Asia. Regional capacity from AI clouds combines the full-stack NVIDIA DSX AI Factory platform , including NVIDIA Vera Rubin, NVIDIA BlueField and NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet networking, giving customers greater choice and control over where workloads and data reside while advancing sovereign computing services and economic growth. Open: Models and Libraries, From Training to Inference Across the ecosystem, AI clouds are expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure and services for developers to build applications with open models and libraries. This new capacity supports model training, fine-tuning for specialized tasks and inference at scale, including applications deployed at the edge. For production inference, Nebius has adopted NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX, using Spectrum-X Ethernet networking to integrate it with Vera Rubin NVL72 on Nebius Token Factory. The combination will bring faster token generation to latency-sensitive applications and agentic systems through the platform’s managed serverless and dedicated endpoints and familiar application programming interfaces. For robotics and physical AI, Nebius offers a purpose-built AI cloud solution that includes its full-stack Physical AI Workbench. Robotics companies including Rhoda AI , RoboForce and Sereact are building on the platform. The company also launched three NVIDIA retail agent blueprints — covering inventory, store operations, and fine-tuning —- into early access on Nebius infrastructure. Nebius is expanding its cloud services widely across the continent with its Physical AI Living Lab, and in Germany as a computer supplier for the Next Frontier Challenge of SPRIND, the Federal Agency for Breakthrough Innovation. Baseten has developed a specialized model for code-review routing with Nemotron 3.5 Lightning used by CodeRabbit. Through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, CodeRabbit improved routing agreement from 75.8% to 80.7% while reducing estimated inference costs by 50% for the evaluated workload. The results demonstrate how AI developers can customize NVIDIA open models for specialized tasks while improving accuracy and inference efficiency. Fireworks and Era4 are partnering to bring open models to enterprises across the U.K. and Europe. The collaboration combines Fireworks ’ model training and inference platform with direct liquid-cooled capacity powered by NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs at Era4’s Chesterfield facility, supporting plans for enterprise AI solutions in financial services, insurance and life sciences. Mistral is expanding its NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure to support model training, customization and inference. The expansion includes NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure planned for delivery in 2027. Trained on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral -operated European data centers, Mistral Large 4 is the company’s latest frontier multimodal model, advancing capabilities across coding, agentic workflows and multimodal understanding. Verda plans to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin, continuing to promote open weight models with NVIDIA Nemotron and NVIDIA Cosmos already in production, and using the NVIDIA Dynamo open source framework for inference optimization. Safe: Secure Boundaries for AI Agents, From Silicon to Software As developers connect models to tools and business systems, they also need controls over what agents can access and do. Announced at GTC Berlin, the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture with support from AI cloud ecosystem partners. Built on the foundation of NVIDIA OpenShell secure runtime software, the architecture is designed to give organizations full-stack control to deploy AI agents with clear boundaries around what agents can access and do. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 for model inference, NVIDIA Vera CPUs with OpenShell for agent harnesses and tool use, and NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPUs running NVIDIA Sentry for in-silicon enforcement. Each play a distinct role in delivering that control, working together so agents can achieve what they’re meant to do without moving beyond the boundaries people set for them. Partners including Aleria , Baseten , Cassava , CoreWeave , Crusoe , DigitalOcean , Firebird , Fireworks, Firmus , G42 , GMI Cloud , IREN , Lambda , Lightning AI, Nebius , Nscale , Radiant Verda and Vultr are supporting the OpenShell Reference Architecture to enable secure agentic deployments for their customers. Together, European AI clouds are connecting regional infrastructure investment with the work of building and deploying AI. Expanded capacity gives builders more places to run workloads.

events.title: Europe’s Industrial Leaders Reinvent Engineering and Manufacturing With NVIDIA
events.summary: To increase productivity, accelerate innovation and create new opportunities for economic growth, Europe’s industrial leaders are tapping NVIDIA CUDA-X and Omniverse libraries , as well as NVIDIA Cosmos and Nemotron open models, across the engineering and manufacturing lifecycle. Bringing those capabilities together on the factory floor, the NVIDIA Factory Operations Blueprint (FOX) is now available in early access on GitHub , providing a path for developers to build and deploy always-on factory manager agents that coordinate work across machines, and specialist agents focused on use cases such as visual inspection, root cause analysis, report generation and fleet management. These agents can connect to frontier models, including NVIDIA Cosmos and Nemotron, and foundational knowledge including computer-aided design, product lifecycle management, simulation software, and IT and operational technology systems. Building on the FOX blueprint enables the ecosystem to build industrial agents that monitor factory operations in real time, correlate visual findings and machine logs to investigate problems, and coordinate responses. With Cosmos in-context learning, these agents can adapt using examples and documentation, without fine-tuning. Siemens is integrating agents built using FOX into Intelligence Center X, its agentic enterprise system, to help identify root causes and coordinate factory operations, for estimated cost savings of 20%. Siemens’ Process Preparation X agents use NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory tools and skills to generate defect images for circuit-board inspection. At its Erlangen electronics factory, Siemens used this approach to reduce calibration time of inspection processes by 40%. Accelerating Engineering From the First Design NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries accelerate simulation, giving engineers faster feedback to explore design alternatives before committing to physical prototypes. At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA is releasing cuDSS for general availability , accelerating the demanding calculations behind the complex simulations of structural stress, fluid flow, electromagnetic fields and semiconductor device behavior. Mercedes-Benz uses Siemens’ Simcenter STAR-CCM+ running on NVIDIA GPUs to compare vehicle designs through faster aerodynamic simulations. In factories, the company applies NVIDIA Cosmos 3 and the Metropolis VSS blueprint to build agents for vehicle inspection and windshield assembly verification, detecting deviations and ensuring consistently high quality. Cadence is benchmarking automotive fluid-dynamics workloads on NVIDIA GPUs to assess opportunities for faster design iteration, while Autodesk brings the NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo and Warp frameworks into NavPack, integrated with Autodesk Alias, to help designers like those at Bentley’s predict vehicle performance and iterate faster using simulation-trained AI. imec and Infineon are accelerating semiconductor simulation with Synopsys software and NVIDIA accelerated computing. Benchmarks of S-Litho on imec’s model show up to 40x speedup, while Infineon uses Sentaurus Device with NVIDIA CUDA libraries to achieve a 12x speedup in 3D breakdown simulation for next-generation power devices. Leonardo is working with Neural Concept on AI-driven aircraft design, tapping NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to bring aircraft geometry and aerodynamic simulation results together. Car manufacturers use Dassault Systèmes ’ LEO & AURA Virtual Companions, powered by NVIDIA Nemotron, and orchestrating CATIA AI Agents & SIMULIA AI Agents with SIMULIA solvers, accelerated by NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, to rapidly design and virtually test vehicle doors before building physical prototypes. UniversalAGI is working with Saab to protect sailors from life-threatending wave impacts at sea, using UniversalAGI’s Latent Interaction Field Transformer physics AI foundation models with accelerated processing by NVIDIA Warp to evaluate thousands of wave conditions and headings in real time instead of days. These capabilities enable vessels to anticipate dangerous motion and autonomously select safer routes to avoid putting sailors at risk, while NVIDIA Omniverse libraries help visualize vessel behavior at sea. PhysicsX is working with GB1, Britain’s America’s Cup team , on AI-powered yacht design, using NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to visualize hull geometry and pressure fields, while Fermioniq ’s Sofia agent helps Deltares and Dutch ministries model river flow by translating natural-language requests into simulation solvers built on NVIDIA Warp. Mistral plans to use CUDA-X, Warp and Omniverse libraries to accelerate physics simulation and generate training data for engineering AI models. Testing Factories and Robots Virtually NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac libraries enable digital twins and robotics simulation , helping manufacturers evaluate production systems and robot behavior before making changes on the factory floor. Audi uses a battery-production digital twin built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to test production concepts before physical equipment is available. The company is also working with Dassault Systèmes and Agile Robots to simulate and validate mobile humanoid robots and logistics processes in DELMIA virtual twins built with Omniverse libraries. Schaeffler is integrating digital twins of its humanoid actuators — components that move robot joints — with NVIDIA Isaac simulation frameworks, helping its robotics partners evaluate component behavior in simulation and reduce physical testing. At Volkswagen Sachsen’s Transparent Factory, Wandelbots uses NOVA with Isaac Sim , built on Omniverse and OpenUSD, to validate assembly workflows digitally and prepare applications for physical robots. Falkor , a KONGSBERG company, is integrating agents and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries into its platform. With Microsoft Azure NCv6 virtual machines powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, agents with spatial intelligence combine engineering data, operating information and 3D equipment geometry to see, simulate and reason over industrial facilities, supporting inspection and maintenance use cases across the process and energy industries. The same simulation approach extends to AI infrastructure. Schneider Electric , together with AVEVA , is developing an AI factory digital twin built for Nscale with Omniverse libraries to help engineers compare power, cooling and equipment configurations before making physical changes. Explore NVIDIA technologies for industrial AI . Watch NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s GTC Berlin Keynote Wednesday, Oct. 21 11 a.m.-1 p.m.

events.title: NVIDIA cuDSS Now Generally Available to Accelerate Engineering and Scientific Simulations
events.summary: NVIDIA cuDSS, launched today in general availability, is an NVIDIA CUDA-X library that shifts a critical part of engineering and scientific simulations onto GPUs. Complex engineering feats — from advanced chips to aircraft to industrial systems —– depend on simulation to predict how designs will perform before they’re built. As designs become more complex, simulations take longer to run, increasing computing demands and limiting the number of ideas teams can test. NVIDIA cuDSS accelerates solving large sparse systems — the math-heavy step that repeats throughout engineering and scientific simulations and often limits how many designs a team can test — by tapping into GPUs. This lets applications reduce time to results and increase simulation throughput, enabling end users to explore larger more realistic models, more accurate representations and a wider design space at a reduced cost. Industry leaders are already integrating NVIDIA cuDSS into their tools to transform workflows for their end customers: Applied Materials: With cuDSS, Applied Materials accelerated sparse solves in Ginestra, its physics-based, defect-centric simulation platform, by up to 10x versus CPU-only approaches, speeding exploration of semiconductor materials and device reliability. COMSOL: Using COMSOL Multiphysics with NVIDIA cuDSS on NVIDIA accelerated computing, ZEISS SMT achieved a measured 4x speedup in an EUV lithography plasma simulation benchmark, completing the full simulation in six days and 14 hours. Cadence : Uses cuDSS in its Celsius software to accelerate simulations of heat, structural stress and warpage in advanced chips and 3D chip designs, helping customers including Nokia analyze complex designs faster. Dassault Systèmes : Dassault Systèmes reports an 8-10x speedup using cuDSS within its Abaqus structural and computer simulation technology electromagnetic solvers for performance-critical simulations across industries. Siemens : Siemens uses cuDSS in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ to accelerate simulations of structures in fluid-structure interaction workflows. Synopsys : Synopsys uses cuDSS in its Sentaurus Device simulator tool to accelerate simulations of advanced logic, memory and power chips, helping Infineon model increasingly complex devices faster. As simulation workloads grow in size and complexity, cuDSS can scale out of the box from individual workstations to large computing clusters. Developers can integrate cuDSS into existing engineering, scientific and optimization software offerings, bringing GPU acceleration to tools already used by engineers and researchers. They can use cuDSS through C, C++, Python and Fortran interfaces. Learn more about cuDSS by visiting the NVIDIA demo booth and Dassault Systèmes booth at GTC Berlin. events.title: NVIDIA Confidential Computing Expands, Enabling Frontier Model Builders to Securely Scale Across Global Infrastructure
events.summary: NVIDIA builds tools to enable safe agents across the stack . The NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, announced today , is part of NVIDIA’s growing portfolio of technologies that enables organizations to safely deploy agents at scale. NVIDIA Confidential Computing is the infrastructure layer that protects the models and data those agents depend on while running. Today, NVIDIA is expanding that layer with Confidential Bare Metal, a new deployment option with NVIDIA Confidential Computing that enables frontier model builders to run sensitive workloads on dedicated third-party infrastructure while retaining control of their models and data. NVIDIA is introducing new platform security controls that protect data in transit, measure platform integrity and enforce hardware-level access restrictions. These new controls let frontier model builders use bare-metal instances to own and operate their bespoke software stack, including host and platform infrastructure software, when operating on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure across third-party cloud, neocloud and enterprise infrastructure. NVIDIA Confidential Computing now offers a converged security architecture with three deployment options: Confidential Bare Metal for bare-metal infrastructure Confidential Containers for Kubernetes environments Confidential Virtual Machines for virtualized environments Organizations can match the right model to their trust boundaries and operating requirements. NVIDIA Confidential Computing is also expanding across NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Rubin systems and will integrate with NVIDIA DSX OS as a reference architecture for cloud providers building AI factories. Confidential Bare Metal gives supported providers a path to serve high-value workloads that require strong model and data privacy protections. For model builders, the expanding ecosystem offers more geographic, sovereign and operational options for scaling training and inference worldwide. Cohere plans to integrate Confidential Bare Metal into Cohere Model Vault, using NVIDIA Confidential Computing trusted execution environments to extend hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU — protecting models and data in memory and across interconnects during execution. “Enterprises trust Cohere to provide a secure and confidential platform for inference,” said Phil Blunsom, chief technology officer at Cohere. “With NVIDIA Confidential Computing in Cohere Model Vault, we’re extending hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU, protecting customer data in memory and across interconnects during execution.” Google Cloud is extending support for Confidential Bare Metal to A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems. These will combine non-virtualized NVIDIA accelerated computing with cryptographic protection for training data and model intellectual property. “Google Cloud introduces Confidential Bare Metal to provide AI labs with hardware-isolated, non-virtualized compute environments and end-to-end cryptographic protection. Our A4X instances, built using NVIDIA Confidential Computing, preserve the privacy of user data, protect model IP, provide top-line serving performance,” said Andrés Lagar-Cavilla, distinguished engineer and AI infrastructure security lead at Google Cloud. Confidential Computing Expands Across the NVIDIA Platform NVIDIA Confidential Computing uses hardware-rooted isolation and cryptographic attestation to help protect models and data during execution. Support now extends to NVIDIA Grace Blackwell NVL72 — bringing Confidential Computing to NVL72 rack-scale systems — as well as x86-based NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 and NVIDIA DGX Rubin NVL8 systems. CoreWeave , Firmus , GMI Cloud , Google Cloud , IREN , Lambda , Microsoft Azure Infrastructure, Nebius , Nscale and Vultr support NVIDIA Confidential Computing deployments. Global systems partners including Cisco , Dell Technologies , HPE , Lenovo, Supermicro and Bull will support these capabilities with NVIDIA-Certified Systems . NVIDIA DSX OS will support all NVIDIA Confidential Computing modes, giving cloud providers a software foundation for building and operating AI factories that support confidential workloads. Learn more about NVIDIA Confidential Computing . events.title: NVIDIA Advances Isaac Platform for General-Purpose Robotics With New Reference Humanoid, Frameworks, Simulation Pipelines and Data
events.summary: News Summary:  Agile Robots announces Agile ONE SN , a humanoid reference platform built on NVIDIA Isaac GR00T and NVIDIA Jetson Thor with planned integration of the NVIDIA Halos safety stack, giving developers and researchers a complete platform for frontier humanoid development and validation. NVIDIA Isaac platform adds new Isaac OS runtime, Isaac Lab 3.0 for robot learning and open source reference workflows that combine ChatGPT Astra with NVIDIA Isaac and Cosmos on NVIDIA DGX Station to accelerate robot data generation, training and evaluation. Europe’s robotics ecosystem, including leaders like ABB Robotics, Flexion, Hexagon Robotics, Humanoid, KUKA, NEURA Robotics, Sereact and Universal Robots, is building on NVIDIA’s open robotics platform to advance autonomous robotic systems.    GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced a major expansion of the NVIDIA Isaac™ open robotics development platform , adding a reference humanoid, datasets and runtime, along with updates to its robot learning framework. Together, these technologies give developers an integrated path from data to deployment to bring general-purpose robots to the real-world faster. “General-purpose robotics is advancing at extraordinary speed — the ChatGPT moment for robotics is fast approaching,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “With NVIDIA Isaac, our full-stack open robotics platform, we are giving developers the models, data, simulation tools and computing systems to bring physical AI to the world’s largest industries.” Agile ONE SN — A Frontier Humanoid Reference Platform for Research Agile Robots announced Agile ONE SN , a full-stack reference humanoid preconfigured with NVIDIA Isaac GR00T and powered by the NVIDIA Jetson Thor ™ edge AI platform. Robotics researchers and developers often struggle to integrate the separate simulation, training and deployment tools needed to take robot skills from development to the physical world. Agile ONE SN unifies these tools and workflows on a single platform, cutting setup time from weeks to days. Agile ONE SN features: Agile ONE S humanoid body, standing 1.40 meters (4.59 feet tall) and weighing 40 kilograms (88 pounds), with 31 degrees of freedom and a 3-kilogram payload per arm. Dual WUJI Hand 2 five-finger hands, each offering 20 degrees of freedom, 1kHz force control and tactile sensing for dexterous manipulation NVIDIA Jetson Thor onboard compute, delivering 2,070 FP4 teraflops of compute and 128GB of unified memory for onboard reasoning and real-time control. Multimodal sensing , including head and wrist cameras, lidar sensors and inertial measurement units to help the robot perceive and interact with its surroundings. NVIDIA Isaac GR00T platform, which comprises the GR00T foundation model, a full workflow from data capture to deployment and whole-body control for coordinated movement. Safety capabilities, with planned integration of on-robot safety protocols with the NVIDIA Halos full-stack safety system for robotics.   “The breakthrough for humanoids is usefulness at scale: one adaptable machine that learns many skills and works across environments built for people,” said Zhaopeng Chen, founder and CEO of Agile Robots. “Today, Agile Robots introduced Agile ONE SN, a full-stack, open reference humanoid built on NVIDIA Isaac GR00T, powered by Jetson Thor, giving developers a ready system to create, train and validate the capabilities needed to put humanoids to work.” Scheduled to be available in early 2027, Agile ONE SN is designed to advance frontier humanoid research and development, with interest from leading institutions such as Stanford University and ETH Zurich. New NVIDIA Technology Accelerate Robot Learning — From Data to Deployment New NVIDIA technologies help developers generate training data, scale robot learning, build simulation environments and deploy robot applications, reducing time to solution. SimReady Central Library offers more than 2,000 simulation-ready robotics and factory assets, while the Human 1M Dataset includes diverse human activities, synchronized three-view video and 3D hand tracking. Both are available on Hugging Face, with the full Human 1M Dataset accessible to Cosmos Coalition partners. NVIDIA Isaac Lab 3.0 is now generally available , providing an open source, agent-ready learning framework training and refining robot policies from desktop to data center using multi-GPU workflows and physics engines including Newton and NVIDIA PhysX ™. NVIDIA Isaac OS , an open source runtime framework built on NVIDIA Holoscan , connects AI, sensors, controls and robot hardware for deterministic, real-time performance from simulation to physical robots. NVIDIA is releasing three open source reference workflows for NVIDIA DGX Station ™ that help developers refine GR00T 1.7 models with reinforcement learning, train dexterous manipulation skills in NVIDIA Isaac Lab and post-train NVIDIA Cosmos ™ world models for synthetic data generation using ChatGPT Astra. NVIDIA Halos provides a full-stack safety platform built on NVIDIA IGX Thor ™ to help move autonomous vehicles and robots from development to safer real-world deployment at scale.   SimReady Central Library on Hugging Face includes simulation-ready assets from Comau , FANUC, ForgeCAD, Franka Robotics, LG Electronics, Palatial, Robotiq, Standard Bots, Universal Robots and Vertiv. NVIDIA’s open source robot learning reference workflows running on DGX Station will be supported by solutions from 1X, Agile Robots, Humanoid, Maven Robotics, Mentee, MicroAGI, Rhoda, Sereact and Skild AI. Robotics partners are integrating NVIDIA Halos within their safety architectures, including Agile Robots , Agility, Dexory , FORT Robotics and KION for warehouse robot safety. SICK is evaluating Halos to advance dynamic safety for industrial robots, helping them respond to changing conditions beyond fixed zones. Advantech and NexCOBOT are developing NVIDIA IGX-based industrial computing platforms, while Reynolds & Moore, Accenture and TÜV SÜD are accelerating the certification process for the safe deployment of industrial physical AI. European Robotics Leaders Build on NVIDIA Open Technologies ABB Robotics is integrating NVIDIA Omniverse™ libraries with RobotStudio HyperReality to simulate and virtually commission robotic systems before installation across a wide range of industries. KUKA Group is using Omniverse libraries in its Visual Components FactoryLens to add real-time rendering for factory simulation workflows. Sereact is using Isaac GR00T with Cosmos Transfer to train and post-train its Cortex platform for goods handling, running on Universal Robots industrial robot arms. Using Jetson Thor, Holoscan Sensor Bridge, Halos and NVIDIA Isaac OS, Humanoid is developing and validating robot behaviors before industrial pilot

events.title: ‘Jackdaw means we pay our mortgages’: relief in Aberdeen over gasfield approval
events.summary: Few believe decision will bring back city’s boom years, but workers hope it will secure North Sea jobs for now UK approves Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea What does the UK’s approval of Jackdaw mean? As recently as 2012, Aberdeen boasted the highest concentration of millionaires in the UK. An ATM reportedly had the highest withdrawal rate in Europe in the 90s, as oil and gas wealth flowed through the city. House prices soared in the scramble for space as fossil fuel firms transformed the city’s grand granite houses into company offices. But that was then. Today, “for sale” and “to let” signs punctuate the city’s main thoroughfares. Disposable income in Aberdeen has fallen by nearly 20% between 2013 and 2023 – more than any other large UK city – after a 2014 oil price shock sparked a brutal reversal in Aberdeen’s fortunes. events.title: European Mobility Leaders Build Safe Vehicles and Robotaxi Fleets on NVIDIA Hyperion
events.summary: News Summary: Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets, with Volvo Cars adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack for safe automated driving. NVIDIA introduces Halos SAFE, a new framework within the NVIDIA Halos safety system, which combines simulation and physical testing to help developers generate measurable, traceable AV safety evidence. NVIDIA announces Alpamayo 2 Edge, Alpamayo Agentic Factory and new Cosmos 3 Nano model variants to help developers build, customize and evaluate autonomous-driving for diverse vehicles, operating conditions and regions. GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced that leading automakers in Europe and mobility providers, including Bolt with Lucid , Mercedes-Benz , Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride, are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets. In addition, Volvo Cars is adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack software for safe automated driving. NVIDIA also introduced new AI and safety technologies to help developers build, validate and deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) at scale. Autonomous transportation represents a multitrillion-dollar opportunity, with robotaxis leading the move to commercial level 4 deployment. NVIDIA Hyperion and the NVIDIA Halos full-stack safety system give automakers and mobility providers the computing performance, safety foundation and long-term support to bring AVs and robotaxi fleets to market at scale. “Robotaxis are the first mass-market application of robotics and physical AI, reinventing how people and goods move,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “NVIDIA Hyperion, together with our Halos safety operating system, gives our partners a full-stack robotaxi platform designed to achieve full autonomy and the highest levels of safety, bringing us closer to a future where everything that moves is autonomous.” Mobility Leaders in Europe Build on NVIDIA Hyperion Automakers and mobility providers in Europe are pursuing various paths to autonomy, from passenger vehicles and robotaxi fleets to autonomous freight trucks. NVIDIA Hyperion’s modular architecture supports all of these programs, compatible with NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack autonomous driving software as well as partners’ own driving software. Bolt has selected NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack for its European robotaxi program, beginning with future Lucid vehicles built on Hyperion. Bolt and NVIDIA will adapt the software for European roads and integrate it into vehicles from multiple manufacturers, combining NVIDIA’s driving and safety technologies with Bolt’s fleet-management systems, operations and local market expertise. Bolt plans to begin gathering real-world driving data to support the development and validation of the autonomous driving technology — subject to regulatory approval — in Madrid in 2027, with Germany being a priority for future deployment as part of a planned European rollout of at least 25,000 level 4-capable future Lucid vehicles built on NVIDIA Hyperion. At GTC Berlin, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles is presenting its autonomous ID. Buzz AD vehicle platform with Hyperion to support multiple autonomous-driving systems. Hyperion provides a common computing and sensor architecture designed to simplify integration and validation, helping developers and mobility operators bring robotaxi and commercial transport services to market. Volvo Cars is combining its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with Hyperion, Halos OS and Alpamayo Stack to enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door. Mercedes-Benz is extending its partnership with NVIDIA on Hyperion and Alpamayo Stack to support the development of the automaker’s L3 and L4 capabilities. The company also announced that MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO, developed in partnership with NVIDIA, will soon get approval for urban point-to-point urban driver assistance in Germany, helping drivers navigate journeys through complex city traffic. Beyond passenger vehicles and robotaxis, Einride is building its next-generation Einride Driver on Hyperion for autonomous freight trucks, using Halos, Alpamayo and NVIDIA Cosmos ™ open world models to develop and validate its driving system, while TIER IV and the Technical University of Munich plan to integrate Hyperion to develop and validate systems for autonomous public transportation in Germany. NVIDIA technology and manufacturing partners are also helping expand the AV ecosystem, with Aptiv , Valeo and Schaeffler building Hyperion-based computing platforms that can be integrated by vehicle manufacturers for L4 AVs and robotaxis. Scaling Safe Autonomy With NVIDIA Halos Halos provides the safety foundation for NVIDIA’s AV platform, bringing together AI computing, safety software and validation from development through deployment. To give developers repeatable ways to evaluate driving behavior and simulation accuracy, NVIDIA today introduced Halos SAFE — the Safety Assurance Framework for Evaluation — with dSPACE , IVEX and TÜV Rheinland collaborating on evaluation workflows. Halos SAFE connects simulation, software- and hardware-in-the-loop evaluation, on-road testing and fleet monitoring through defined scenarios, tests and measurable performance criteria to generate traceable safety evidence that supports deployment. The Halos SAFE ecosystem also includes JLR, Mercedes-Benz, Volvo Cars, 51Sim, aiMotive , AVL, Deepen AI , Foretellix and Synopsys. Accelerating AV Development Developing AVs means teaching AI to handle the diversity of real-world driving, then bringing that intelligence into the vehicle. NVIDIA’s latest models, tools and blueprints help developers prepare driving data, improve models and evaluate performance: Alpamayo 2 Edge , a 2-billion-parameter reasoning model built on NVIDIA Cosmos, is optimized for the NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor™ platform and designed to run at 10Hz for in-vehicle scene understanding and motion planning. AlpaJudge , a human-calibrated evaluation and reward model, scores driving explanations to assess reasoning quality, filter weak annotations and reduce manual review of training data. Foundation4D labels multicamera video without lidar input, supporting perception-model training and NVIDIA Omniverse™ NuRec scene reconstruction. New Cosmos 3 Nano model variants expand synthetic data generation and closed-loop simulation for autonomous driving through synchronized multiview, multi-camera and lidar generation across diverse driving scenarios. events.title: Healthcare and Life Sciences Leaders Build on NVIDIA to Advance Drug Discovery and Expand Patient Care
events.summary: News Summary: NVIDIA and the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design debut RFD4-Proteina, a new open model that combines programmable protein design with search capabilities, unlocking new frontiers in biology. Siemens Healthineers is advancing the next generation of adaptive radiotherapy, using NVIDIA intelligence to increase access to life-saving cancer care with agentic co-planning, patient-specific simulation and robotic control. Automata, Benchling, Biolevate, Boltz, Danaher, Hologen and Therna Biosciences are using the NVIDIA BioNeMo open platform to develop scientific agents that connect drug design, autonomous laboratories and biological discovery, helping researchers move from hypothesis to experiments faster. GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced collaborations with leading global healthcare and research organizations to advance protein design — including through a newly released open model, RFD4-Proteina — accelerate drug discovery and bring greater precision to cancer care. Life sciences researchers must search vast biological design spaces and aim to shorten the cycle between computational design and laboratory testing to discover new medicines. Cancer care teams face a different challenge: translating complex imaging and treatment data into precise plans for each patient. NVIDIA open models, accelerated computing and physical intelligence can help experts evaluate more possibilities faster, from designing new proteins to planning adaptive radiotherapy. “Agentic and physical AI are opening new possibilities across medicine, from designing proteins and powering autonomous laboratories to improving personalized cancer care,” said Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare at NVIDIA. “Together with healthcare and life science leaders, we’re accelerating scientific discovery and advancing more precise, accessible care around the world.” NVIDIA and the UW Institute for Protein Design Introduce RFD4-Proteina Proteins are molecular tools that perform many of life’s essential tasks, and designing new versions could open paths to new medicines, diagnostics and industrial applications. But finding a protein capable of performing a designed function requires searching an immense range of possible designs. NVIDIA and the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design are debuting RFD4-Proteina, a new NVIDIA BioNeMo™ open model that combines programmable protein design with search capabilities. The model generates targeted protein designs, enabling scientists and agents to search and refine designs using molecular inputs, constraints and scoring objectives. Potential applications include designing proteins to interrupt disease processes or detect signs of disease in diagnostic tests. In testing reported in the research draft, RFD4-Proteina achieved higher computational design success rates and generation throughput than the evaluated baselines across four benchmark suites: protein binding, small-molecule binding, enzyme scaffolding and DNA binding. The model helps researchers explore and prioritize candidates for laboratory testing, where experiments establish how a design performs under tested conditions. “We are moving from an era of discovering the proteins nature has made to one in which we can design entirely new ones,” said David Baker, 2024 Nobel Laureate in chemistry and director of the Institute for Protein Design at the University of Washington. “RFD4-Proteina expands what scientists can create, from proteins that could advance drug discovery to enzymes that break down pesticides. Making the model open will allow researchers around the world to build on these capabilities and pursue solutions once beyond the reach.” RFD4-Proteina is available today through partners including Amazon Bio Discovery, Anthropic’s Claude Science, Benchling, Databricks , Google Cloud, Hugging Face, Nebius, OpenAI and Tamarind Bio, enabling researchers and developers to integrate the open protein design model into agent, cloud and scientific computing workflows. Siemens Healthineers Advances Cancer Care With NVIDIA Siemens Healthineers and NVIDIA are collaborating to develop the next generation of adaptive radiotherapy with agentic and robotic intelligence, combining imaging and oncology expertise with accelerated computing and simulation to simplify workflows and expand access to care. By 2050, approximately 35 million people worldwide are projected to be diagnosed with cancer each year. Care teams face growing pressure to deliver precise, personalized treatment while managing limited specialist capacity. Greater efficiency can help expand access to care while maintaining the precision needed to deliver prescribed doses to tumors and protect surrounding healthy tissue. Siemens Healthineers is working with NVIDIA to further develop adaptive radiotherapy through agentic co-planning, patient-specific simulation and real-time computing. NVIDIA Nemotron ™ open foundation models are being explored to power agentic co-planning, with the aim of helping oncologists evaluate and refine personalized treatment strategies. The models could then be combined with NVIDIA CUDA ® -accelerated dose calculation for rapid patient-specific simulation and the NVIDIA Holoscan platform to connect live sensor data with AI and simulation to support adaptive treatment. “Adaptive radiotherapy is built on a single principle: treatment should adapt to the patient, not the other way around,” said Arthur Kaindl, head of Varian, the Siemens Healthineers cancer-care business. “We’ve made important advances in precision and adaptation — most recently, with the launch of the Accela system. Our collaboration with NVIDIA builds on that progress, exploring how AI and real-time computing could give clinicians greater speed and insight to make informed decisions, adapt treatment with greater confidence and deliver personalized care to more patients.” Scientific Agents Advance Drug Discovery and Development Life sciences is one of the world’s most important scientific frontiers, with global scientific R&D reaching $3.8 trillion and annual pharmaceutical budgets approaching $300 billion. events.title: NVIDIA, Nokia and Leading Telecom Operators Turn Networks Into Distributed Intelligence Platforms
events.summary: News Summary: Leading global telecom operators are expanding NVIDIA-powered computing across their networks to deliver advanced services closer to people and businesses, improve wireless experience and automate network operations. T-Mobile completes the world’s first AI-RAN call on a commercial network, while BT, Deutsche Telekom and Elisa announce AI-RAN pilots on live networks using Nokia’s CUDA-accelerated anyRAN software on NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer, and NVIDIA introduces new Aerial RAN Computer configurations for high-capacity sites. Nine EMEA telecom operators are building and expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure across centralized and distributed locations. Operators and software partners are adopting NVIDIA Nemotron open models to deliver agentic services and develop agents for autonomous network operations.   GTC Berlin— NVIDIA today announced that leading global telecom operators are turning their networks into distributed intelligence platforms, adding NVIDIA accelerated computing to centralized data centers, metro sites and cell sites so they can serve models and applications closer to the people, businesses and machines that use them. T-Mobile has completed the world’s first AI-RAN call on a live network in Bellevue, Washington, with NVIDIA and Nokia. Deutsche Telekom is advancing physical AI for industries, and Orange is introducing new voice intelligence services for enterprises and emergency responders. Elisa has completed Europe’s first field trial of AI-RAN, running voice, mobile data and vision AI together on a single accelerated computing platform over 5G, and BT is preparing live AI-RAN trials in the U.K. Nokia is bringing its anyRAN software on NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer (ARC) for trials at BT, Deutsche Telekom, Elisa and Orange. Nine operators across Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) are building or expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure, while Nokia and Cisco are incorporating NVIDIA Nemotron ™ open models into the software operators use to run autonomous networks. “Telecom networks were built to carry the world’s conversations. Now, they will also carry the world’s intelligence,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “Leading global operators are turning their land, power and connectivity into a distributed AI infrastructure — bringing intelligence closer to the industries, people and robots that use it. With Nokia, we’re extending accelerated computing into the radio network itself, creating the foundation for AI-native 5G.” Intelligence is built in five layers : land, power and shell, chips, infrastructure, models and applications. Telecom operators already own sovereign infrastructure at the first layer, with data centers, regional sites and cell sites that have power, fiber and spectrum. By adding NVIDIA accelerated computing, open models and applications on top, operators are building the full intelligence stack into their networks. At distributed sites, a common converged platform based on the AI-RAN architecture can serve open models, power robotics, voice and agentic applications, and run intelligent 5G software. Europe’s Leading Telcos Build Distributed Infrastructure Infrastructure sits at the foundation of telecom’s transition to distributed service platforms. Deutsche Telekom plans to expand its NVIDIA-powered Industrial AI Cloud, which hosts open models — including NVIDIA Nemotron and Soofi — and serves robotics companies such as Agile Robots. At distributed sites, Deutsche Telekom is piloting AI-RAN trials with Nokia and NVIDIA, and demonstrating NVIDIA ARC to run inference between the device and the network edge. A GTC Berlin demonstration with Agile Robots shows the approach: on-robot intelligence handles real-time perception and action, a model at the distributed edge supports fine-tuning and coordination across robots, and the central infrastructure provides capacity for larger training workloads. Orange is hosting open models, including NVIDIA Nemotron, as a managed service on top of its Live Intelligence trusted AI platform, enabling new advanced services for enterprises. At distributed sites, Orange is deploying NVIDIA ARC for voice intelligence applications using Nemotron Speech, demonstrating new services to help emergency and field services teams translate across multiple languages in real time with low latency and reliability. Elisa has deployed NVIDIA ARC at a distributed network location, running a voice intelligence application that serves as an enterprise assistant, and is using open models to build edge applications. EMEA telcos are building or expanding NVIDIA-powered infrastructure: New infrastructure: CRA in the Czech Republic, etisalat in the United Arab Emirates, Silknet in Georgia and TIM in Italy. Expansions: Cassava in Africa, Deutsche Telekom in Germany, Fastweb + Vodafone in Italy, Kazakhtelecom in Central Asia and Orion Telecom in Serbia.   AI-RAN Brings Accelerated Computing Into the Radio Network AI-RAN extends accelerated computing into the radio access network (RAN), turning it into an intelligence workload that runs on the same platform as advanced services, so operators can get more out of their spectrum while serving demand from sites close to users. Globally, nearly 20 telecom operators have publicly announced AI-RAN collaborations using Nokia anyRAN software and NVIDIA ARC. T-Mobile recently marked the world’s first AI-RAN call on its commercial network in Bellevue, Washington, running on commercial ARC servers, Nokia’s NVIDIA CUDA-accelerated RAN software and massive multiple-input multiple-output radios, and connected to an existing 5G Standalone core and a commercial smartphone. BT is planning live AI-RAN trials in Birmingham, England, with Nokia and NVIDIA in 2027. Deutsche Telekom has validated Nokia and NVIDIA’s commercial AI-RAN platform in Bonn and Oulu labs, including AI-enhanced uplink channel estimation to improve uplink user throughput, with plans to move to field trials in 2027. Elisa simultaneously ran voice, mobile data and video analytics on the NVIDIA ARC platform, marking a European first in Elisa’s over-the-air field environment using 5G spectrum. The trial clears the way for distributed deployment and commercial AI-RAN services in 2027. Orange is testing Nokia 5G software on NVIDIA ARC, focusing on AI-RAN spectral efficiency improvements and support for edge services in live networks.   NVIDIA is introducing two ARC configurations — MGX 2U and MGX 4U — designed for dense, high-capacity intelligence and radio workloads, typically deployed at centralized RAN sites. Powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO™ 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs , the configurations will offer x86 and NVIDIA Vera CPU options. Dell Technologies , Quanta Cloud Technology and Supermicro will offer ARC-ready servers. Open Models Power

events.title: Dubai records strong sales for homes valued at over $10m as it attracts wealthy despite Iran war
events.summary: Dubai recorded 86 residential transactions valued at $10 million or more during the third quarter this year, down 17 per cent annually, as wealthy investors continued to invest in the emirate despite the Iran war. Among the deals, 13 were for homes valued at more than $25 million, property consultancy Knight Frank said in its latest report on Wednesday. Of the total, the 73 that were in the $10 million to $25 million bracket had a combined value of Dh3.93 billion ($1.07 billion), with the remaining 13 transactions generating Dh1.84 billion. The highest-value transactions accounted for about 15 per cent of sales for more than $10 million by number, but nearly 32 per cent of their total value. “Despite the exceptional geopolitical backdrop across the region, Dubai’s luxury homes market has continued to record high volumes of sales during Q3, albeit these are lower than this time last year,” said Faisal Durrani, partner and head of research, Mena at Knight Frank. Prices across the city’s 10 prime neighbourhoods have dipped for the first time since 2020, declining by 5 per cent between the second and third quarters, he said. In total, prime transaction volumes are 29.4 per cent lower than this time last year. “The biggest drag at the moment on overall market activity is the ongoing regional conflict . The somewhat ‘stop-start’ nature of the hostilities is predictably a confidence dampener,” Mr Durrani said. Wealth inflows Dubai and Abu Dhabi continue to attract wealthy individuals on the back of government initiatives that support economic growth, including favourable tax environments, business-friendly policies and significant infrastructure investment. Net wealth in the UAE is set to jump to $6 trillion by the end of this decade despite the short-term volatility caused by the Middle East conflict , a report this month by Boston Consulting Group found. In the five years to the end of 2030, net wealth in the Emirates is set to increase by more than $2.3 trillion, at an annual growth rate of 10.6 per cent, the report said. Dubai and Abu Dhabi have also been ranked among the top 10 destinations for next-generation wealth despite current war-related concerns, Savills said in a report this week. Dubai was ranked eighth and the capital 10th among favoured cities for the $84 trillion of wealth expected to be transferred between generations over the next two decades, it said. In the first nine months of the year, a total of 412 transactions worth $10 million or more were recorded in Dubai, up 15 per cent on an annual basis, Knight Frank's latest report found. The combined value of the deals this year stood at about $6.67 billion, the report said. On a quarterly basis, transaction volumes in the third quarter were down about 34 per cent from the previous period, the report said. Palm Jumeirah tops list In terms of areas of Dubai, Palm Jumeirah recorded the most residential sales worth $10 million or more in the third quarter, with 27 transactions worth Dh2.01 billion, Knight Frank found. The community accounted for approximately 31 per cent of luxury homes sold between July and September and 35 per cent of their total value. “The easing of prices by 9.1 per cent over the last 12-months means the island is increasingly offering ‘good value’ at Dh4,083 per square foot,” said Louis Harding, partner and head of UAE residential at Knight Frank. “Buyer interest here continues to largely stem from those seeking a permanent or holiday home, rather than buy-to-flip investors.” Jumeirah ranked second by transaction volume, followed by Emirates Hills, Dubai Hills Estate and Jumeirah Golf Estates.
